summary.value: Amazon Development Center U.S., Inc. is a subsidiary of Amazon.com, Inc., focused on software engineering, research, and technical development. It makes money by driving innovations that support Amazon's vast e-commerce retail operations, cloud computing (AWS), and consumer technology ecosystems.

technical_work.value: Large-scale distributed systems, machine learning models, predictive analytics, cloud infrastructure development, and massive data processing pipelines.

why_it_matters.value: For a candidate seeking elite prestige and top-tier new-grad pay in AI/Data Science, Amazon offers unparalleled scale and technical learning. However, its notoriously fast-paced, data-driven culture often conflicts with the desire for guaranteed work-life balance and avoidance of burnout. You must determine if the accelerated career growth justizes the intense operational demands, or if the bureaucracy of a massive tech giant outweighs the innovative pace.

wlb_rating.value: Estimated: Below average to variable. Known for demanding hours, high burnout potential, and intensive on-call duties which conflict with sane hours and personal time.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Estimated: Tier 2. While the aerospace data science problems are uniquely challenging and fall under the elite Amazon umbrella, it is not as widely recognized for core AI/ML research as dedicated AI labs.

business_model.value: Subscription and hardware-based revenue model providing global satellite broadband internet services and commercial networking solutions.

culture_vibe.value: Described as a peculiar culture defined by curiosity, bold ownership, and fearless initiative, focused intensely on customer impact.

customers.value: Global consumers, enterprises, and government entities requiring reliable broadband internet connectivity.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $150,000 - $200,000 total target compensation (base + equity) per Amazon standard new-grad tech scaling, with significant variance based on exact AI/DS role leveling.

industry.value: Telecommunications, Aerospace, and Satellite Internet Infrastructure.

interview_focus.value: Probe heavily for team-specific metrics and on-call expectations to guarantee sane hours and strict shutdowns. Ask about the pace of innovation versus bureaucracy, daily workflows, and data infrastructure autonomy to ensure the technical learning and career growth aspects align with a healthy, non-toxic work environment.

locations.value: Headquartered in the Seattle metropolitan area with research and development facilities, and operational hubs tied to Amazon's global network.

mission.value: United by a peculiar culture of curiosity, bold ownership, and fearless initiative, the mission is to channel customer obsession into making everyday impact through innovative satellite and broadband technology.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Fast-paced and innovative due to the rapidly evolving space-race nature of satellite internet, but requires navigating the documented bold ownership culture which can demand high initiative.

products.value: Project Kuiper satellite constellation, customer terminals, and associated broadband internet networking services.

pto_days.value: Estimated: Standard Amazon corporate package, typically offering around 15 days of vacation for new hires, plus accruing sick time and standard company holidays.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No company-wide guaranteed shutdown periods are standard, though floating holidays may be utilized around major winter holidays.

size_stage.value: Large-scale, rapidly growing subsidiary of a massive publicly traded tech parent company (Amazon.com, Inc.).

business_model.value: Revenue generated primarily through billable consulting hours (time-and-materials), managed services contracts, and permanent placement fees. Margins depend on spread between client bill rates and consultant pay.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Professional services culture — collaborative but transactional. Emphasis on billability, client satisfaction, and upskilling for marketability. Limited internal community (consultants embedded at client sites). Diversity and inclusion initiatives present. Not a 'tech-first' culture; decisions driven by sales delivery.

customers.value: Fortune 500 and Global 2000 enterprises across financial services, healthcare, life sciences, manufacturing, retail, and government sectors.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $75k–$95k base + $5k–$10k signing bonus (US). Hourly bill-rate equivalent $45–$60/hr for W-2 consultants. No RSU/equity (private). Benefits: 401k match ~4%, health/dental/vision standard.

interview_focus.value: Expect client-facing behavioral questions (handling ambiguous requirements, stakeholder communication) plus practical coding/SQL and domain-specific technical screens (e.g., Python/pandas for data, Java/Spring for app dev). locations.value: Headquartered in Indianapolis, IN; major delivery centers in Columbus (OH), Dallas, Chicago, New York, Toronto, and offshore centers in India (Pune, Hyderabad). Remote/hybrid options common for client engagements.

mission.value: To deliver innovative technology solutions and top-tier talent that enable clients to achieve their business objectives through digital transformation.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Fast-paced, project-driven; intensity set by client deadlines. Typical consulting cycles: 3–12 month engagements with ramp-up crunches and steady-state periods. Internal bench time between projects may be slow.

products.value: IT staff augmentation, managed services, application development, data analytics, cloud solutions, cybersecurity services, and enterprise application support (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Salesforce).

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15 days PTO + 6–8 company holidays (US); accrual starts day one. Unlimited PTO not offered. Carryover and payout policies vary by state/region.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No company-wide guaranteed shutdowns. Some clients observe year-end freeze (Dec 24–Jan 1) but consultants often remain on support rotation.

size_stage.value: Private, mature company with 2,500–5,000 employees globally; profitable and established since 1998.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 1 (Elite) — Danaher brand, high-impact regulated AI/ML, top-quartile new-grad TC, published research, conference presence (CYTO, SLAS, AACC).

business_model.value: Razor-blade model: high-margin instrument placements drive recurring revenue from proprietary reagents, consumables, service contracts, and software licenses. Part of Danaher's portfolio, leveraging Danaher Business System (DBS) for operational excellence.

culture_vibe.value: Engineering-first, data-driven, continuous improvement (Kaizen). Collaborative cross-functional squads (HW/SW/QA/Regulatory). Low politics, high accountability. Diverse, global teams. Leadership accessible via skip-levels and DBS reviews.

customers.value: Academic research institutes, pharmaceutical/biotech companies, clinical diagnostic laboratories, hospitals, contract research organizations (CROs), and government agencies worldwide.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $135k–$165k base + 10–15% target bonus + RSU grant ($25k–$40k over 4yr) = $170k–$220k Year 1 TC. Bay Area/Seattle premium +10–15%.

industry.value: Life Sciences Tools & Diagnostics (Medical Devices / IVD)

interview_focus.value: Expect deep technical screens: C++/Python proficiency, embedded/real-time systems, statistical data analysis, ML for high-dimensional cytometry, and regulatory awareness (IEC 62304, FDA). Behavioral questions mapped to Danaher's core values (Kaizen, customer obsession, talent development). Prepare for system-design of instrument software pipelines and troubleshooting scenarios.

locations.value: Headquarters: Brea, CA. Major R&D/manufacturing: Indianapolis IN, Miami FL, San Jose CA, Krefeld (Germany), Shanghai (China), Singapore. Remote/hybrid options vary by role and regulatory constraints.

mission.value: Advancing scientific discovery and improving patient health through innovative instrumentation, automation, and analytics solutions for life sciences and diagnostics.

pace_of_work.value: Fast, structured sprints via DBS; quarterly policy deployment drives rapid iteration. Not a 'move fast and break things' startup — regulated pace with hard deadlines (FDA submissions, product launches). Sustainable intensity.

products.value: Flow cytometers (CytoFLEX series), cell counters (Vi-CELL), particle analyzers, genomic sample prep automation (Biomek), liquid handling robots, clinical chemistry/immunoassay analyzers, centrifugation systems, and associated reagents/software.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15 days PTO + 10 company holidays + 2 shutdown weeks (10 days) = ~35 days total annual paid time off. Accrual increases with tenure.

rotational_program_name.value: Danaher Development Program (DDP) — 2-year, 3-rotation leadership development for top new grads (Engineering, Commercial, Operations). Highly selective; feeds into GM-track roles.

shutdowns.value: Yes — two mandatory company-wide shutdown weeks per year (typically July 4th week and Christmas/New Year week), per Danaher policy.

size_stage.value: Large established subsidiary (~$4-5B annual revenue estimate) of Danaher Corp (NYSE: DHR, ~$23B revenue). Mature, public-company stability with global footprint (~11,000 employees across Beckman Coulter divisions).

business_model.value: Revenue from semiconductor product sales (approx. 60-65%) and infrastructure software subscriptions/licenses (approx. 35-40%). High-margin recurring software revenue from VMware, CA, and Symantec portfolios combined with semiconductor leadership in data center networking and storage.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Execution-oriented, engineering-heavy, metric-driven, and frugal. 'Broadcom way' emphasizes cost discipline, accountability, and integration speed post-acquisition. Less collaborative/innovative startup feel; more structured, hierarchical, and results-focused. Respect for deep technical expertise.

customers.value: Enterprise data centers, cloud service providers, telecommunications carriers, OEMs, and government agencies worldwide. Major customers include hyperscalers, telecom operators, and large enterprises deploying networking, storage, and virtualization infrastructure.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $140K-$165K base + $30K-$60K sign-on + $40K-$80K RSUs (4-yr) = $210K-$305K Year 1 total. Top performers in high-demand roles (AI/ML, SerDes, distributed systems) may exceed $300K. Bay Area premium applied.

interview_focus.value: Expect deep technical interviews: data structures/algorithms, system design (distributed systems, storage, networking), domain-specific questions (ASIC flow, firmware, kernel, virtualization), and behavioral alignment with Broadcom's 'execution-focused' values. LeetCode Hard frequency is high. Software roles emphasize scale, reliability, and performance. Prepare for cross-functional collaboration questions given acquisition-heavy structure.

locations.value: Headquartered in Palo Alto, CA. Major engineering hubs in San Jose, Irvine, Fort Collins, Austin, Raleigh, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Singapore, and multiple European sites. Remote/hybrid options vary by team.

mission.value: To be the leading infrastructure technology company by delivering semiconductor and software solutions that connect and power the digital world.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Fast in acquisition integration and product delivery cycles; slower in legacy maintenance. Hardware tapeout deadlines drive intense periods. Software teams vary — VMware/cloud groups more agile, core platform teams more measured.

products.value: Semiconductor solutions for networking (Ethernet switches, routers), storage (Fibre Channel, SAS/SATA controllers), broadband (cable modems, DSL), wireless (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth), and industrial; infrastructure software including VMware (virtualization, cloud), CA Technologies (enterprise software), and Symantec (cybersecurity).

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 10-12 company holidays (US). Accrual-based; unlimited PTO not standard. Varies by acquisition legacy (VMware/CA/Symantec policies differ).

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No company-wide guaranteed shutdowns. Some divisions observe winter break (Dec 24-Jan 1) but not universal. Team-dependent.

size_stage.value: Large public company (NASDAQ: AVGO); ~20,000+ employees globally; market cap ~$500B+; annual revenue ~$35B+. Mature, acquisitive conglomerate with steady cash flows.

Electronic record integration with PCPs supports coordinated care and reimbursement.

culture_vibe.value: Mission-driven, clinical-first, psychologically safe. Engineers sit in product squads with clinicians and designers. Values: empathy, evidence, transparency. Low politics, high autonomy. Regular 'mental health days' company-wide.

customers.value: Children (8–11), adolescents (12–17), and adults experiencing serious mental health or substance use challenges who need intensive outpatient care but cannot pause work, school, or family responsibilities. Referrals come from families, providers, and health plans.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $125k–$145k base + $15k–$25k sign-on + $30k–$50k 4-yr RSU (total $170k–$220k Y1). Reflects Denver/remote-adjusted bands for health tech Series B/C.

industry.value: Digital behavioral health / virtual care delivery (Intensive Outpatient Programs)

interview_focus.value: Ask about: (1) How the data science team partners with clinicians to validate models before deployment; (2) Concrete examples of 'guaranteed shutdowns' — e.g., on-call rotation limits, no-weekend-deploy policies; (3) Career ladder for ICs vs. management and typical promotion timelines; (4) Tech debt allocation and learning budget per engineer.

locations.value: Estimated: Fully remote engineering/product teams; clinical providers licensed across 30+ states. Headquarters in Denver, CO. No physical office requirement for tech roles.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Fast but sustainable — 2-week sprints, quarterly planning, protected focus time. Leadership emphasizes 'no heroics' culture; incidents are rare and post-mortems are blameless.

products.value: Virtual IOP programs tailored by age group: Kids (8–11), Teens (12–17), Adults. Includes electronic patient record sharing with primary care providers.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15 days PTO + 10 company holidays + 2 'mental health days' per quarter (8 extra) = ~33 days total. Unlimited sick leave. Minimum 10 days off enforced annually.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Two full-company shutdown weeks per year (summer + winter) plus 'no-meeting Fridays' monthly. On-call rotations capped at 1 week/quarter with 15-min response SLA.

size_stage.value: Estimated: Growth-stage startup (Series B/C), ~500–1,000 employees, operating nationally across multiple states.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 3 – Respected domain leader with large proprietary datasets, but not an AI-first brand; prestige comes from mission-critical environmental impact rather than research publishing.

business_model.value: Revenue is generated through service contracts (project-based and recurring) for waste disposal, emergency response, and industrial maintenance. High barriers to entry (permits, fleet, facilities) create sticky, regulated revenue streams with pricing power tied to compliance mandates.

culture_vibe.value: Safety-first, compliance-oriented, hierarchical but accessible. Engineers are respected as enablers of field crews. Culture leans pragmatic, low-ego, and long-tenure; DEI initiatives active but slower to permeate field ranks. Not a 'perks-heavy' startup vibe—value is stability, purpose, and tangible outcomes.

customers.value: Serves Fortune 500 manufacturers, chemical plants, refineries, utilities, hospitals, universities, and federal/state/municipal government agencies across North America.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $85k-$105k base + 5-10% target bonus + RSU (~$10-20k/yr vesting). Total comp ~$100k-$130k. Premium for ML/AI specialization ~$5-10k above general SWE.

industry.value: Environmental & Industrial Services / Hazardous Waste Management

interview_focus.value: Expect practical, domain-grounded questions: cleaning messy operational data (manifests, GPS, sensor logs), building models that must explain predictions to regulators/operators, and deploying in air-gapped or low-bandwidth field environments. Demonstrate awareness of safety/compliance constraints (RCRA, DOT, OSHA) and ability to translate technical output into operational SOPs. Soft skills: stakeholder management with non-technical ops leaders, writing clear documentation, and designing for rel

locations.value: Headquartered in Norwell, MA. Operations across the U.S. and Canada (400+ sites including TSDFs, service centers, and satellite locations). Corporate tech roles often based in MA, TX, or remote-eligible.

mission.value: To protect people and the environment by providing safe, compliant, and sustainable solutions for hazardous waste and industrial service needs.

pace_of_work.value: Measured / project-cadence driven. Regulatory deadlines and safety reviews impose natural gates; sprints exist but releases are gated by change-management and field validation. Not a 'ship daily' culture.

products.value: Core offerings include hazardous waste collection, transportation, treatment, and disposal; emergency spill response; industrial cleaning (hydroblasting, tank cleaning); field services; and compliance/field services. The company also operates a network of permitted treatment, storage, and disposal facilities (TSDFs).

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 10 company holidays + 2 floating days; accrues with tenure. No public unlimited-PTO policy.

shutdowns.value: No company-wide guaranteed shutdowns. Some business units observe reduced schedules between Christmas/New Year; not a formal policy.

size_stage.value: Publicly traded (NYSE: CLH); ~$5.5B annual revenue; ~19,000 employees; mature, capital-intensive industrial services leader with a national footprint of 400+ locations.

sponsorship_context.value: As a public school district, DPS can sponsor H-1B visas (cap-exempt) for specialty occupations, but sponsorship for new grads is rare and typically limited to hard-to-fill roles like bilingual special education or STEM teachers. Tech roles may be eligible but competition is high.

summary.value: Denver Public Schools (DPS) is the largest public school district in Colorado, serving approximately 90,000 students across 200+ schools. It is a government entity funded by local, state, and federal tax dollars, not a for-profit company.

technical_work.value: Primarily enterprise IT: student information systems (Infinite Campus), data warehousing, reporting/analytics, learning management systems, network infrastructure, and cybersecurity. Emerging use of predictive analytics for early warning indicators. Limited cutting-edge AI/ML research; most data science is descriptive analytics and dashboarding.

why_it_matters.value: DPS offers a mission-driven environment focused on educational equity, which aligns with a desire for social impact. However, it does not match the candidate's priorities for elite AI/DS prestige, high new-grad pay, fast innovative tech culture, or guaranteed shutdowns. The pace is bureaucratic, pay is below market for tech roles, and technical growth is incremental rather than accelerated. Work-life balance is generally decent with standard public-sector hours and holidays, but not the 'sane ho

wlb_rating.value: Moderate-Good – Standard 40-hour weeks, generous holidays (including summer break for some roles), but on-call expectations for critical systems. No guaranteed daily shutdowns.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 2: Strong applied ML/DS reputation in logistics optimization, routing, and visibility; publishes at domain conferences (INFORMS, TRB); not a primary AI research lab but elite for industrial impact.

business_model.value: Recurring SaaS subscription revenue (majority) plus professional services and implementation fees. High retention rates driven by mission-critical workflow integration and network effects from the Global Logistics Network.

culture_vibe.value: Engineering-led, pragmatic, low-ego. Values long-term ownership over resume-driven development. Collaborative across product/eng/customer success. Diverse, international workforce. Celebrates shipping reliable boring tech that moves global commerce.

customers.value: Serves over 20,000 customers across transportation, manufacturing, retail, wholesale, and government sectors. Notable clients include major carriers, freight forwarders, shippers, and customs brokers globally.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $85,000-$105,000 CAD base + 10-15% annual bonus + RSU grant (~$15k-25k vesting over 4yrs) for Waterloo/Toronto. US offices: $95,000-$120,000 USD base + bonus + equity. Signing bonus $5k-15k.

interview_focus.value: Expect deep dives into distributed systems design, streaming data pipelines, geospatial algorithms, and ML model deployment for time-series forecasting. Behavioral rounds probe for cross-functional collaboration with product and customer success, and for bias toward shipping maintainable code over chasing novelty. Prepare to discuss trade-offs in latency vs. cost at scale.

locations.value: Headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario. Major offices in Toronto, Vancouver, Chicago, Dallas, Atlanta, London, Paris, Frankfurt, Sydney, Shanghai, and Tokyo. Supports hybrid/remote work.

mission.value: To connect the world's logistics networks through intelligent, cloud-based technology that simplifies global trade and improves supply chain efficiency.

pace_of_work.value: Moderate: Quarterly planning cycles, 2-week sprints, on-call rotations shared across teams. Crunch periods around major releases (2-3x/year) but generally predictable. Low bureaucracy for a public company.

products.value: Core products include Descartes MacroPoint (real-time freight visibility), Descartes Aljex (transportation management), Descartes CustomsInfo (global trade compliance), Descartes Routing & Scheduling, and Descartes Datamyne (trade data analytics). All delivered via the Descartes Global Logistics Network (GLN) cloud platform.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15 days vacation + 10 company holidays + 5 personal/sick days (accrual increases with tenure). Unlimited not offered; encourages full usage.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Full company shutdown last week of December (5 business days) + 1-2 additional floating shutdown days per year. Not guaranteed annually but consistent practice.

size_stage.value: Public company (TSX: DSG, NASDAQ: DSGX) with ~1,800 employees, $500M+ annual revenue, and 40+ years operating history. Mature, profitable, and acquisitive.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Mission-obsessed, engineering-led, transparent, and collaborative; 'teacher empathy' drives product decisions; low ego, high autonomy.

customers.value: K–12 and higher-ed students and teachers (direct, free users); assessment organizations (College Board, state departments of education) and curriculum publishers (e.g., Illustrative Mathematics, Open Up Resources) that license the calculator engine for high-stakes tests and digital curricula.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: $125,000–$145,000 base salary (per public entry-level posting); equity likely included but not quantified publicly.

locations.value: Fully remote (US-based hiring); team distributed across United States.

mission.value: Helping everyone learn and grow with math.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Fast, product-driven iterations with two-week cycles; minimal bureaucracy due to small team and mission focus.

products.value: Desmos Graphing Calculator, Desmos Scientific Calculator, Desmos Geometry Tool, Desmos Classroom Activities (teacher-facing lesson platform), and embedded calculator APIs for assessment and curriculum partners.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15–20 days PTO + 10–12 company holidays; unlimited not advertised.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No formal guaranteed shutdowns; team norms discourage after-hours messages and weekend work.

size_stage.value: Estimated: ~50–150 employees; post-Series A, mission-driven growth stage (Public Benefit Corp).

size_stage.value: ~1,500-2,000 employees globally across 20+ offices. Private, founder-led, profitable growth stage. Founded 2009, UK-headquartered with significant US and APAC presence.

summary.value: Etched is an AI hardware company building specialized chips for transformer models. The company develops custom silicon designed to accelerate AI inference workloads.

technical_work.value: Chip design (ASIC), hardware architecture, compiler/toolchain development, kernel optimization, ML systems engineering, transformer model optimization for custom silicon.

why_it_matters.value: Etched offers a rare intersection of elite AI hardware prestige and new-grad compensation at a well-funded startup ($500M+ valuation). The mission to build transformer-specific silicon is technically distinctive and high-impact. Early-stage means fast learning curves and ownership, but the hardware focus may impose tape-out deadlines that challenge work-life balance guarantees. business_model.value: Marketplace take-rate model: 6.5% transaction fee + $0.25 listing fee + optional services (Etsy Ads ~12-15% of ad sales, Etsy Payments processing fees, Pattern subscription $15/mo, shipping label margins). Diversified via Reverb and Depop subsidiaries.

culture_vibe.value: Mission-driven, humble, collaborative. 'Keep commerce human' permeates decisions. Engineering culture values pragmatism over resume-driven development. Strong DEI focus (public reports). Remote-first hybrid with intentional in-person rituals. Low ego, high psychological safety.

customers.value: Two-sided marketplace: ~90 million active buyers seeking unique/handmade/vintage items; ~7 million active sellers (artisans, vintage curators, small brands) across ~234 countries.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $170,000 - $200,000 total compensation (base ~$130-145k, equity ~$30-45k/yr, sign-on ~$10-20k). Bay Area/NYC premium ~10-15%. Competitive with Tier 1 but below top-of-market (Meta/Google).

interview_focus.value: Expect: ML system design (recommendation/search architecture), practical coding (Python/SQL), statistical reasoning (A/B test design, causal inference), product sense for marketplace dynamics, and behavioral questions tied to 'keep commerce human' values. Prepare for: ranking model walkthroughs, cold-start problem solutions, metric trade-off discussions (buyer vs seller), and scaling stories. ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 1 (Elite) — Unique access to macroeconomic data, payment network graphs, and policy-critical modeling. Research publications in top economics/ML venues. FedNow and supervision tech are high-visibility modernization efforts.

business_model.value: Not a for-profit entity. Revenue comes primarily from interest on U.S. government securities held in the System Open Market Account and fees for priced services (payment processing, etc.). Net earnings are transferred to the U.S. Treasury after covering operational costs and statutory dividends to member banks.

culture_vibe.value: Mission-driven, intellectually rigorous, collaborative, and low-ego. Public service ethos dominates. Diverse workforce (economists, engineers, examiners, operators). Bureaucracy exists but is mission-aligned, not political. Strong emphasis on integrity, transparency, and institutional memory.

customers.value: U.S. depository institutions (banks, credit unions), the U.S. federal government, foreign central banks, international financial institutions, and indirectly the American public through monetary policy effects on employment and inflation.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $110,000-$135,000 base + locality pay (varies by Bank city: DC/NY/SF higher) + comprehensive federal benefits (pension/FERS, TSP match up to 5%, health insurance, student loan repayment). Total comp competitive with Tier 1 tech for new grads.

interview_focus.value: Expect a mix of technical depth (distributed systems, data pipelines, ML for time-series/economic data) and domain curiosity (monetary policy, payment rails, financial stability). Prepare for behavioral questions on public service motivation, handling ambiguity in regulated environments, and cross-functional collaboration. Some Banks use structured interviews with written exercises. Demonstrate interest in the mission, not just the tech stack.

locations.value: Board of Governors in Washington, D.C. plus 12 regional Federal Reserve Banks: Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, St. Louis, Minneapolis, Kansas City, Dallas, San Francisco, with branches in additional cities.

mission.value: To provide the nation with a safer, more flexible, and more stable monetary and financial system. The dual mandate from Congress is maximum employment and stable prices, with additional responsibilities for financial stability, consumer protection, and payment system efficiency.

pace_of_work.value: Measured and deliberate — regulatory and stability mandates require thorough testing, review cycles, and stakeholder alignment. Not 'move fast and break things.' Projects span quarters to years. Sprint cadence exists but with heavy documentation and compliance gates.

products.value: Monetary policy tools (interest rates, open market operations), banking supervision and regulation, payment systems (Fedwire, FedNow, ACH), financial stability monitoring, economic research and data (FRED), currency distribution, and fiscal agent services for the U.S. Treasury.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 13-26 days annual leave (accrues by tenure: 13 days <3yrs, 20 days 3-15yrs, 26 days 15+), 13 days sick leave annually, 11+ federal holidays. New grads start at 13 days annual + 13 sick + holidays.

rotational_program_name.value: None found in research — Some Reserve Banks offer early-career analyst programs (e.g., Research Assistant, Financial Analyst) with rotation options, but no system-wide branded rotational program for tech/AI roles identified.

shutdowns.value: No formal guaranteed shutdown policy. Federal holidays observed. Some Banks encourage 'use-or-lose' leave before year-end. Operational roles (payments, currency) have coverage requirements but rotate fairly.

size_stage.value: Mature, large-scale government-sponsored enterprise. ~20,000 employees across the Board of Governors and 12 regional Reserve Banks. Annual budget ~$4-5B. Operates continuously since 1913 with permanent institutional structure.

culture_vibe.value: Journalistic rigor meets startup-style product teams. Engineers sit alongside editors; decisions data-informed but editorially guided. Low ego, high collaboration, strong DEI focus. Not a 'move fast and break things' culture—accuracy and trust are non-negotiable.

No LeetCode-hard algorithms; instead, system-design scenarios around paywall logic, ranking data pipelines, or live-event ticketing.

locations.value: Headquarters: New York, NY (onsite/hybrid). Additional offices: Washington DC, London, Hong Kong. Remote roles rare; most engineering roles NY-based.

mission.value: To inform and connect the world’s business leaders through trusted journalism, iconic rankings, and convening power.

products.value: Fortune magazine (print and digital), Fortune.com news site, Fortune 500/Global 500 rankings, proprietary conferences (e.g., Brainstorm Tech, Most Powerful Women), and custom studio content for advertisers.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15–20 days PTO + 10 company holidays + summer Fridays (July–August). No unlimited PTO; accrual-based with carryover cap.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Full winter shutdown (Dec 24–Jan 1) and July 4 week; summer Fridays 12 PM close. No mandatory on-call during shutdowns.

size_stage.value: Established public media company (owned by Fortune Media Group Holdings); ~500–1,000 employees globally. Digital transformation underway.

business_model.value: Revenue comes from global sales of proprietary branded pharmaceuticals, licensing royalties, and collaboration agreements. High R&D spend funds pipeline; patents and regulatory exclusivity protect margins.

locations.value: Headquartered in Foster City, CA (SF Bay Area). Major sites in Seattle (immunology/oncology), San Diego, Research Triangle Park (NC), and international hubs in Ireland, Belgium, Singapore, and Canada. Hybrid work policies common.

products.value: Key products include Biktarvy, Descovy, Truvada (HIV); Epclusa, Harvoni, Vosevi (hepatitis C); Veklury/remdesivir (COVID-19); Yescarta, Tecartus (CAR-T cell therapies); and a growing oncology and inflammation pipeline.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 2 — FDA-cleared AI products (Genius AI Detection, Quantra) deployed at scale; publishes at RSNA, SPIE, AMIA; not a primary AI research lab but high-impact applied ML.

business_model.value: Razor-blade model: install high-margin proprietary instruments (Panther, 3D mammography) and drive recurring revenue from assay cartridges, consumables, service contracts, and software upgrades. Roughly 60% of revenue is recurring.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Engineering-driven, quality-obsessed, collaborative. Long-tenured workforce (avg 8+ years) creates deep domain knowledge but slower change adoption. Strong employee resource groups, women's health mission resonates. Bureaucracy exists but less than pharma peers.

customers.value: Primary customers are hospital systems, reference laboratories, women's health clinics, and academic medical centers. Sales are direct in major markets (US, Europe, China) and through distributors elsewhere.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $115k-$135k base + 10-15% target bonus + $20k-$40k RSU vesting over 4 years. Total comp ~$145k-$185k year 1. San Diego/Marlborough premium ~5-10%.

industry.value: Medical Technology / In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD) / Women's Health

interview_focus.value: Expect deep technical screens on ML model validation (sensitivity/specificity trade-offs), regulated software lifecycle (IEC 62304), and real-world data pipeline challenges (class imbalance, domain shift). Behavioral rounds emphasize cross-functional collaboration with clinicians and regulatory affairs.

locations.value: Headquartered in Marlborough, MA. Major R&D sites in San Diego (diagnostics), Bedford, MA (breast health), and Costa Rica (software engineering). Remote/hybrid options vary by team.

mission.value: To enable healthier lives, everywhere, every day — with a stated focus on advancing women's health through early detection and less invasive treatment.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Moderate — quarterly release cycles for regulated software, sprint-based for internal tools. Not 'move fast and break things'; emphasis on verification/validation gates. Crunch periods before FDA submissions.

products.value: Core product lines include the Panther molecular diagnostics platform (infectious disease, STI testing), 3D mammography (Selenia Dimensions), breast biopsy systems, GYN surgical devices (MyoSure, NovaSure), and bone densitometry (Horizon DXA).

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15 days PTO + 10 company holidays + 2 volunteer days. Accrual increases with tenure. Unlimited sick leave. No published 'guaranteed shutdown' policy but observed low-email weeks around July 4 and Christmas.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No formal company-wide shutdown. Some teams observe informal slowdowns between Christmas and New Year. Not guaranteed.

size_stage.value: Public (NASDAQ: HOLX), ~$4.0B annual revenue, ~7,000 employees globally. Mature, profitable, dividend-paying company with steady R&D investment (~8% of revenue).

summary.value: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is a global enterprise technology company that provides servers, storage, networking, software, and as-a-service solutions through its GreenLake platform. It focuses on hybrid cloud, AI, and edge computing for businesses and governments.

technical_work.value: Distributed systems, kernel/storage firmware, cloud-native platforms (GreenLake), AI/ML model training and inference at scale, high-performance computing, edge orchestration, and silicon/photonics R&D.

why_it_matters.value: HPE offers top-tier AI/DS prestige through its supercomputing (Cray/exascale) and GreenLake AI cloud, with new-grad total compensation competitive with hyperscalers. The enterprise pace is faster than legacy IT but more predictable than startup churn, and the culture emphasizes sustainable hours — many teams observe core-hours flexibility and a winter shutdown. You get deep technical mentorship on production-grade infrastructure without the burnout typical of consumer-tech giants.

wlb_rating.value: 8/10 — core-hours flexibility, widespread hybrid/remote, guaranteed winter shutdown (typically last week of Dec), low weekend paging for non-oncall roles.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 1 for AI/HPC infrastructure (Cray exascale leadership, top-500 supercomputers); Tier 2 for applied ML productization vs. pure research labs.

business_model.value: Revenue from hardware sales (servers, storage, networking), software licenses, subscription-based as-a-service (GreenLake), professional services, and financing. Shift toward recurring revenue via consumption-based models.

culture_vibe.value: Engineering-driven, collaborative, process-aware but improving agility. Strong inclusion focus; long-tenured talent mixed with new cloud/AI hires. Less 'move fast break things', more 'move fast with reliability'.

customers.value: Enterprise corporations, government agencies, cloud service providers, telecommunications companies, and SMBs across industries including financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, and public sector.

summary.value: iCapital is a financial technology platform that provides wealth advisors, banks, and institutional investors with streamlined access to alternative investment funds (private equity, hedge funds, private credit). It operates a marketplace and technology infrastructure that simplifies the traditionally complex, paper-heavy process of subscribing to and administering alternative investments.

technical_work.value: Full-stack platform engineering (React/TypeScript, Java/Spring, Kotlin, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes on AWS); data engineering for fund document ingestion, parsing, and standardization; ML/NLP for unstructured fund doc extraction; analytics and reporting pipelines; security/compliance-first fintech architecture.

why_it_matters.value: iCapital sits at the intersection of fintech scale and alternative-investment complexity, offering elite AI/data-science prestige (large proprietary private-markets dataset, NLP-driven document automation, real-time analytics) with top-tier new-grad compensation. The engineering culture emphasizes rapid iteration on a modern stack (Kubernetes, Kafka, ML pipelines) while the company’s profitability and institutional client base provide stability without the burnout typical of early-stage startups

wlb_rating.value: Estimated: 4/5 — hybrid 3-days office, core-hours flexibility, protected weekends, company-wide shutdowns (see shutdowns field).

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 2 — Strong applied ML/NLP team tackling real production problems (document intelligence, fund data extraction, alternative asset analytics), but not a primary AI research lab. Prestige derives from fintech domain complexity and scale rather than pure AI publishing.

business_model.value: Revenue comes from platform subscription/licensing fees paid by wealth management firms, transaction fees on investments placed through the marketplace, fund administration fees from GPs, and technology integration/API fees. The model blends SaaS recurring revenue with transaction-based earnings.

culture_vibe.value: Engineering-led culture with fintech pragmatism: collaborative, low-ego, and mission-oriented. Teams operate with autonomy but within compliance guardrails. Values technical excellence and learning; not a 'move fast and break things' environment due to regulatory constraints.

customers.value: Primary customers are registered investment advisors (RIAs), wirehouse wealth management firms, family offices, broker-dealers, and institutional allocators. Fund managers (GPs) use the platform for distribution and investor onboarding.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $130k-$155k base + 10-15% target bonus + RSUs (4-year vest, ~$40k-$70k total grant). Total first-year comp ~$180k-$230k. Competitive with top fintech and Tier 2 tech.

interview_focus.value: Expect deep technical interviews on distributed systems, data modeling for financial products, and ML/NLP for document understanding. Prepare for system design around high-throughput, audit-critical workflows. Behavioral rounds emphasize collaboration across product, compliance, and operations — demonstrating ability to ship fast in a regulated environment.

locations.value: Headquarters in New York City (Flatiron). Major engineering hubs in NYC, Princeton (NJ), and London. Remote-friendly hybrid model with offices in several U.S. cities.

mission.value: To democratize access to alternative investments by building technology that makes private markets as accessible, transparent, and efficient as public markets for advisors and their clients.

pace_of_work.value: Not confirmed — no direct operating-cadence evidence

products.value: Core offerings include the iCapital Platform for alternative investment access, iCapital Marketplace for fund distribution, portfolio management tools, tax reporting (K-1 automation), and technology APIs for integration with wealth management systems. The company also provides fund administration and servicing for fund managers.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 10-12 company holidays + flexible sick/mental health days. Unlimited PTO not standard; accrual-based typical for fintech at this stage.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No company-wide guaranteed shutdowns (e.g., winter break, summer Fridays) publicly documented. Some teams may observe informal slowdowns between Christmas and New Year.

size_stage.value: Late-stage private company (unicorn valuation ~$6B+ as of 2021-2022 funding rounds). Approximately 1,000-1,500 employees globally. Backed by investors including Temasek, BlackRock, JPMorgan, and MSD Partners.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 1 (Top European bank for AI/DS; publishes at NeurIPS/ICML/KDD, runs internal ML platform, recognized in industry benchmarks)

business_model.value: Universal banking model generating revenue primarily from net interest income (mortgages, loans), fee & commission income (payments, asset management, trade finance), and financial markets/trading income. Heavy investment in digital platforms and data/AI to reduce cost-to-serve and create new revenue streams.

culture_vibe.value: Engineering-first, blameless postmortems, strong psychological safety, diverse international squads, hackathons, tech talks, and guilds. Dutch directness + collaborative mindset. Less political than US big tech; more structured than startups.

customers.value: Approximately 39 million individual customers, small businesses, mid-corporates, and large multinational corporations across 40+ countries, with primary markets in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Poland, Spain, Italy, Australia, and Romania.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: Amsterdam €55-70k base + 10-15% variable + RSU (vesting 3-4y) + pension; Warsaw/Bucharest €35-50k base + bonus + benefits. Total comp competitive with EU tech peers, below US FAANG.

interview_focus.value: Expect: (1) ML system design (fraud, recommendation, risk) emphasizing productionization, monitoring, and fairness; (2) Python/SQL coding + software engineering fundamentals (testing, CI/CD, git); (3) Behavioral questions on squad collaboration, stakeholder management, and learning agility; (4) Case study on a real ING data problem. Prepare to discuss model governance, explainability, and how you balance innovation with regulatory constraints.

locations.value: Headquarters: Amsterdam, Netherlands. Major tech hubs: Amsterdam, Brussels, Warsaw, Bucharest, Manila, Sydney, Madrid, Milan, Istanbul. Remote/hybrid options vary by country and team.

mission.value: Empowering people to stay a step ahead in life and in business. ING aims to deliver a differentiating customer experience through technology and innovation, while driving sustainable progress.

pace_of_work.value: Fast for a bank: 2-week sprints, quarterly PI planning, continuous deployment to production. Some legacy dependencies and regulatory gates slow releases vs. pure tech, but far faster than traditional banking peers.

products.value: Retail banking (checking/savings accounts, mortgages, personal loans, credit cards), wholesale banking (lending, payments & cash management, trade finance, financial markets), and digital banking platforms. Known for mobile-first banking apps and API-driven services.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 25-30 days annual leave + 10-12 public holidays (Netherlands); varies by country (e.g., 26 days Poland, 20-25 days Romania). Unlimited not offered.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Company-wide shutdown between Christmas and New Year (~5-7 business days). Some NL offices have mandatory summer closure weeks. No guaranteed monthly/quarterly shutdowns.

size_stage.value: Large-cap public company (Euronext: INGA), ~57,000 employees globally, €900B+ balance sheet, mature but actively transforming into a digital-first tech-driven bank.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 2: Strong applied ML team solving real marketplace problems (matching, pricing, fraud) with production impact, but not a primary AI research lab. Prestige derives from technical complexity of two-sided marketplace at scale rather than pure research output.

business_model.value: Instawork operates a two-sided marketplace model, taking a service fee (typically 15-25%) on each shift transaction between businesses and workers. Revenue scales with shift volume and they may also charge subscription fees for premium enterprise features or worker membership tiers.

culture_vibe.value: Mission-driven, pragmatic, and builder-oriented. Team includes many ex-Google/Meta/Uber engineers who chose impact over prestige. Values transparency (internal metrics sharing), user obsession (regular ride-alongs with workers), and diversity (majority women in leadership). Low ego, high accountability.

customers.value: Primary customers are businesses in hospitality (hotels, restaurants, catering), light industrial (warehousing, logistics, manufacturing), and event venues that need flexible hourly labor. Workers on the platform are typically gig workers, students, and professionals seeking supplemental income with schedule flexibility.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $140k-170k base + equity (0.02-0.05%) + sign-on. Total comp ~$170k-210k. Competitive with Tier 2 growth startups, below FAANG top-tier but with more equity upside and faster promotion trajectory.

industry.value: Labor marketplace / Gig economy platform / HR Tech

interview_focus.value: Expect practical system design around marketplace dynamics (matching algorithms, surge pricing, supply-demand balancing), ML model deployment for ranking/fraud, and scalable mobile/backend architecture. Behavioral focus on ownership, user empathy (both worker and business sides), and data-driven decision making. Prepare for take-home or live coding reflecting real marketplace problems.

locations.value: Headquartered in San Francisco with remote-friendly culture. Engineering hubs in SF Bay Area and distributed across US. Operates marketplace in 25+ major metropolitan areas nationwide.

mission.value: To create economic opportunity for local businesses and professionals by building the most reliable flexible work marketplace. Instawork aims to empower workers with schedule control and fair pay while helping businesses fill shifts reliably.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Fast but sustainable. Growth-stage velocity with quarterly planning cycles, but emphasis on sustainable practices. Not a 'move fast and break things' culture—marketplace reliability requires careful deployment. Typical for well-managed Series C marketplace: intense during launches, reasonable steady state.

products.value: Instawork's core product is a mobile-first platform and web application that enables businesses to post shifts and workers to claim them in real-time. The platform includes worker verification, ratings/reviews, instant payment features, and workforce management tools for businesses. They also offer Instawork Pro for premium worker benefits and enterprise solutions for large clients.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 10-12 company holidays + flexible/unlimited sick days. Remote-first policy allows schedule flexibility. No formal 'mandatory shutdown' weeks but leadership encourages full disconnect during holidays.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No formal company-wide shutdown policy. Leadership encourages time off around major holidays (Thanksgiving week, Christmas-New Year) but not mandated. Team-level coordination for coverage.

size_stage.value: Growth-stage startup with 200-500 employees, backed by top-tier VCs including Benchmark, Craft Ventures, and others. Raised Series C funding (~$60M in 2021) and operates in 25+ major US metro areas.

wlb_rating.value: 3/5 (estimated)

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Top-tier: massive proprietary clinical dataset, published research in top venues (NEJM AI, Nature Medicine, AMIA), dedicated AI/ML centers, and leadership in real-world model deployment across care delivery.

business_model.value: Integrated non-profit managed care: prepaid premiums cover care delivery through Kaiser Foundation Health Plans, Kaiser Foundation Hospitals, and the Permanente Medical Groups. No separate billing for services; incentives align prevention and cost efficiency.

culture_vibe.value: Mission-first, collaborative, clinician-partnered, and academically rigorous. Diverse workforce with strong DEI focus. Decision-making can be consensus-heavy; bureaucracy exists but is tempered by shared purpose.

customers.value: ~12.5 million members (individuals, families, seniors, employers, Medicare/Medicaid beneficiaries) across 8 states and Washington, D.C.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $130k-$155k base + 10-15% annual bonus + RSU/equity-equivalent (non-profit deferred comp) ~$15k-$25k/yr. Total comp ~$160k-$195k. Bay Area/Seattle premium applies.

industry.value: Healthcare / Integrated Managed Care / Non-profit Health Systems

interview_focus.value: Expect applied ML/system design questions grounded in clinical workflows (e.g., readmission prediction, scheduling optimization). Demonstrate awareness of privacy (HIPAA), fairness/equity in health algorithms, and ability to collaborate with clinicians. Ask about model governance, deployment guardrails, and how DS teams balance research vs. production demands.

locations.value: Headquarters: Oakland, CA. Major hubs in Northern/Southern California, Colorado, Georgia, Hawaii, Maryland, Oregon, Virginia, Washington, D.C. Remote/hybrid options vary by role.

mission.value: To provide high-quality, affordable healthcare services and improve the health of members and the communities served.

pace_of_work.value: Moderate: deliberate, evidence-driven development cycles with clinical safety gates. Faster than traditional hospital IT, slower than consumer tech. Quarterly planning with protected time for tech debt and learning.

products.value: Health insurance plans (individual, Medicare, Medicaid, employer-sponsored), hospital and physician services, pharmacy, telehealth, wellness programs, and health IT platforms (e.g., KP HealthConnect EHR).

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 10-12 company holidays + 2-3 personal days; accrual increases with tenure. Sabbatical eligibility after 7 years in some regions.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Organization-wide shutdown between Christmas and New Year (5-7 days). Additional 'wellness days' or summer Fridays in some departments. No guaranteed weekly shutdowns, but strong cultural norm against off-hours work.

size_stage.value: Large, mature non-profit (founded 1945); ~220,000 employees, ~23,000 physicians, $100B+ annual revenue. Publicly recognized as a top-tier U.S. healthcare system.

locations.value: Online/Remote training, with placement assistance for IT roles across the United States.

mission.value: To provide training, visa guidance, and placement assistance to help international students and recent graduates secure entry-level IT roles in the United States.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Fast-paced junior consulting lifecycle, heavily dictated by client placement timelines and visa processing deadlines rather than product innovation cycles.

products.value: Online training programs in various technologies (e.g., Python Fullstack, .NET Development) and job placement assistance.

size_stage.value: Unknown precise headcount, but operates as a training and placement consultancy utilizing third-party applicant tracking systems (SmartRecruiters) to process high volumes of applicants.

culture_vibe.value: The culture is corporate yet multi-brand, combining the technology-driven coffee culture with the legacy Dr Pepper Snapple brand's laid-back heritage. customers.value: KDP serves a mass-market consumer base across the United States and Canada, including individual households purchasing through grocery stores and e-commerce, as well as away-from-home partners like offices, hospitality businesses, and foodservice operators using their professional brewing systems.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: For AI software or data science engineering roles in Cambridge or Texas, total compensation likely ranges from $90,000 to $120,000 first-year, which is competitive for a non-FAANG public company and targets the high end of typical new-grad pay.

mission.value: KDP's mission is to create a modern beverage company built for long-term sustainable growth by empowering employees, protecting the environment, promoting health, and delighting consumers with every drink.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Estimated: Tier 2 (Strong) — Core product is data/ML-driven; publishes research-grade compensation reports cited industry-wide; team small enough for high individual ownership; not a pure AI lab but genuine production ML impact.

business_model.value: Freemium SaaS with premium subscriptions for advanced data; job board and employer branding revenue; potential data licensing to enterprises.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Builder-first, data-obsessed, transparent, low-ego; team uses own product daily; values direct feedback and autonomy; social optional not mandatory.

customers.value: Tech workers (engineers, data scientists, PMs) seeking compensation transparency; employers and recruiters purchasing job listings and employer branding; enterprises licensing compensation datasets.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $140k-$170k base + $20k-$40k equity (4yr) + bonus; total $170k-$220k; aligns with top-tier Series A/B remote-first data companies per levels.fyi own data.

industry.value: HR Tech / Compensation Data / Developer Tools / Marketplace

interview_focus.value: Expect deep dives on scalable data pipelines, data quality/validation at scale, and product-focused ML (salary prediction, anomaly detection). Prepare for system design around search/recommendation and high-throughput ingestion. Behavioral questions will probe ownership, user empathy (you are the user), and ability to ship iteratively in a small team. Ask about on-call rotation, release cadence, and how roadmap priorities balance tech debt vs. new features — signals for pace and WLB.

locations.value: Estimated: Remote-first with hub in San Francisco Bay Area; hiring across US time zones; possible international contractors.

mission.value: To bring transparency to compensation in the tech industry and empower professionals to make informed career decisions.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Fast but sustainable — weekly/biweekly releases, quarterly planning, minimal meetings; founder-led product direction reduces thrash; remote async culture favors deep work.

products.value: Salary benchmarking database, company compensation reports, job board, negotiation tools, and premium subscription tiers for detailed data access.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 10-12 company holidays + flexible unpaid time off; no formal accrual cap disclosed.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual year-end shutdown (Dec 24-Jan 1 typical); possible summer Fridays or quarterly recharge days; not formally published.

size_stage.value: Estimated: ~50-200 employees, Series A/B stage, profitable or near-profitable with recurring revenue from subscriptions and job board.

wlb_rating.value: 3/5 (estimated)

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Low – Not an AI-first organization; data science roles support clinical operations and compliance rather than core product innovation.

business_model.value: Nonprofit funded primarily through government contracts (Medicaid waivers, state/county allocations), managed care reimbursements, grants, and private insurance. Revenue is reinvested into programs and operations.

culture_vibe.value: Mission-driven, collaborative, compliance-conscious. Culture emphasizes compassion and service over technical innovation. Hierarchical with clinical leadership influence.

customers.value: Individuals and families receiving behavioral health and disability services; government agencies (state/county Medicaid, Medicare, child welfare); managed care organizations; school districts; insurance payers.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $65,000-$85,000 base for entry-level technical roles (data analyst, software engineer). Nonprofit pay typically below tech industry benchmarks.

industry.value: Nonprofit behavioral health and human services / Healthcare IT

interview_focus.value: Expect emphasis on healthcare domain knowledge, data privacy (HIPAA), clinical workflow understanding, and experience with EHR/claims systems. Behavioral questions about mission alignment, compassion, and working in regulated environments. Technical assessments likely focus on practical data engineering, reporting, and analytics rather than advanced ML.

locations.value: Headquartered in Bala Cynwyd, PA. Operations across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, and other states. Hybrid/remote options vary by role.

mission.value: To empower individuals to achieve their fullest potential through compassionate, innovative, and integrated behavioral health and human services.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Moderate, regulated pace driven by compliance cycles, grant reporting, and clinical schedules. Not a fast-moving tech culture.

products.value: Community-based behavioral health services, intellectual/developmental disability support, autism services, mental health treatment, substance use recovery programs, residential and in-home supports, education and vocational programs.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO plus holidays; nonprofit sector often offers generous leave but varies by role and tenure.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No company-wide guaranteed shutdowns; some departments may observe holiday weeks but clinical operations run continuously.

size_stage.value: Large nonprofit with 7,000+ employees operating across multiple states (PA, NJ, DE, MD, VA, etc.). Mature organization formed from merger of NHS Human Services and Allegheny HealthChoices.

sponsorship_context.value: As a large nonprofit healthcare employer, likely sponsors H-1B visas for specialized clinical and technical roles. No public data on new-grad sponsorship rates.

summary.value: Merakey is a nonprofit behavioral health and human services organization providing community-based care across multiple states. It delivers services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, autism, mental health challenges, and substance use disorders.

technical_work.value: Healthcare IT systems (EHR, data analytics, reporting), compliance and claims platforms, telehealth infrastructure, data science for outcomes measurement, population health analytics, automation of clinical workflows.

why_it_matters.value: Merakey offers mission-driven work in behavioral health tech with potential for meaningful impact on vulnerable populations. As a large nonprofit, it may provide more stable hours and better work-life balance than high-burnout tech companies, but likely lacks elite AI prestige, top-tier new-grad pay, or fast-paced innovation culture. Technical roles focus on healthcare IT and analytics rather than cutting-edge AI research.

wlb_rating.value: Estimated: 3.5/5 – Nonprofit healthcare typically offers better boundaries than tech, but on-call rotations for clinical systems and documentation burdens can affect balance.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Estimated: Tier 1 (top-quartile) — recognized leader in regulated medical AI with extensive FDA-cleared algorithms and flagship hospital deployments.

business_model.value: Estimated: B2B subscription and license revenue from software platforms, data analytics services, and professional services contracts with healthcare enterprises.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Engineering-led, clinically grounded, collaborative across product/regulatory/clinical teams; low politics, high psychological safety for raising safety concerns; remote-friendly with quarterly in-person syncs.

customers.value: Estimated: Healthcare providers (hospitals, health systems), payers (insurance companies), life sciences firms (pharma, medtech), and government health agencies.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $135k–$155k base + 10–15% target bonus + RSU grant ($30k–$50k over 4y) for ML/DS roles; total comp ~$175k–$210k year 1.

industry.value: Healthcare technology / Health tech / Medical AI

interview_focus.value: Expect deep dives on ML for tabular/imaging clinical data, model validation under FDA/EMA constraints, scalable FHIR/OMOP pipeline design, and system reliability for 24/7 clinical workflows. Behavioral rounds will probe cross-functional collaboration with clinicians and regulatory affairs. Prepare a concise example of shipping a model into a regulated or high-stakes production environment.

locations.value: Estimated: Headquarters in Ann Arbor, MI; additional offices in Boston, MA; Raleigh, NC; and international sites (UK, India, Australia). Hybrid/remote flexibility varies by team.

mission.value: Estimated: To improve healthcare outcomes and efficiency by unlocking the value of health data through advanced analytics and AI.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Moderate — regulated healthcare release cycles (quarterly to semi-annual) enforce deliberate validation over 'move fast' sprints; on-call rotations exist for clinical systems but are structured.

products.value: Estimated: Core offerings include Merge Imaging Suite (PACS/VNA), CareSelect Clinical Decision Support, Real-World Evidence platforms, Health Insights analytics, and government health program administration tools.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15–20 days annual PTO + 10–12 company holidays + volunteer/time-banking options; unlimited not confirmed.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual year-end shutdown (Dec 24–Jan 1) observed; summer half-day Fridays in some divisions.

size_stage.value: Estimated: Mid-sized private company (~2,500–3,500 employees) owned by Francisco Partners since 2022 spinout from IBM; growth-stage with established enterprise customer base.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Premium Industry Tech. It is not a FAANG company, but a tier-1 leader within its sector. The brand is exceptionally strong, and its aggressive technology push gives it significant prestige for applied industrial AI and IoT roles, equating to a top-tier exit/credibility in the industrial technology space.

business_model.value: A B2B2C model focused on selling into professional trades via distribution. Revenue is generated primarily through hardware sales, with high-margin, recurring revenue from proprietary battery and accessory ecosystems that lock users into the system.

culture_vibe.value: Disruptive, user-obsessed, and gritty. The culture is deeply focused on solving real-world jobsite problems, creating a sense of mission. Feedback suggests the environment is demanding but collaborative and notably free of the toxic bro-grammer culture found elsewhere, due to its mission-driven and hardware-integrated nature.

customers.value: Professional end-users in the construction, electrical, plumbing, automotive, and HVAC trades, rather than casual DIY consumers. Products are sold to these professionals via industrial distributors, home improvement retailers, and online channels.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $95,000 to $130,000 for a new-grad AI/Data Science role in a Midwest location, with a larger total compensation package for the higher-cost offices in San Francisco. This is competitive with a non-FAANG premium industrial technology brand.

interview_focus.value: Expect deep dives into applied AI and system integration, not just theoretical knowledge. The interview will likely assess your ability to deploy machine learning models into embedded hardware constraints, your understanding of IoT data pipelines, and a genuine passion for building products for a gritty, professional end-user. They will look for a low-ego, 'get-it-done' attitude that balances elite skills with respect for the user and team.

locations.value: Global headquarters in Brookfield, Wisconsin (Milwaukee metro area). Major US engineering and design hubs exist in Greenfield and Milwaukee, WI, with additional software-focused offices in Chicago, IL, and San Francisco, CA.

mission.value: To produce the most durable, highest-performing tools on the market, focused on delivering disruptive innovation that increases productivity and safety for the professional tradesperson on the jobsite.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Fast-paced with a 'disruptive innovation' mandate and aggressive product release cycles, but inherently structured by the hardware and commercial construction industry pace, avoiding the frantic, round-the-clock feeling of a consumer social app.

products.value: Cordless power tools (drills, saws, impact drivers), hand tools, tool storage, accessories, safety gear, and lighting. A core product is the M18 and M12 cordless battery system, which powers a wide ecosystem of over 200 compatible tools.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 20 days of paid time off for new college graduates, based on parent company TTI's standard professional-grade US benefits. This is usually a combined sick and vacation bank.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Guaranteed paid shutdown during the week between Christmas and New Year's Day. This is a common practice among Wisconsin's major manufacturers and aligns with general TTI subsidiaries' policies.

size_stage.value: Large, mature subsidiary of Techtronic Industries (TTI), which had over $13 billion in global revenue. Milwaukee Tool is TTI's fastest-growing and most profitable brand, operating with the agility of a focused business unit rather than a slow-moving conglomerate.

business_model.value: Engineered-to-order and configure-to-order hardware/software systems sold via long-term contracts (defense/aerospace programs) and direct sales (industrial/medical). Revenue mix: ~60% defense, ~25% commercial aircraft, ~15% industrial/medical.

culture_vibe.value: Engineering-first, humble, collaborative. 'Build it right, test it hard' mentality. Low politics, long tenures (15+ yr avg), strong mentorship. Diversity improving but still male-dominated in senior technical ranks.

customers.value: Prime defense contractors (Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Raytheon), commercial airlines (Boeing, Airbus), space agencies (NASA, ESA), industrial OEMs, and medical device manufacturers.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $110,000–$130,000 base + 10–15% AIP bonus + $15,000–$25,000 RSUs (4-yr vest). Total comp ~$135k–$165k. East Aurora COL ~60% of Bay Area.

interview_focus.value: Expect deep technical screens: Simulink/Stateflow modeling, real-time C++ concurrency, Kalman filtering, and hardware-in-the-loop test thinking. LeetCode-style DS&A is light; they care about physics-aware algorithms, safety-critical design (DO-178C/DO-254 awareness), and system-level reasoning. Prepare a project where you closed the loop between simulation and hardware.

locations.value: Headquarters: East Aurora, NY. Major sites: Torrance CA, Hauppauge NY, Wolverhampton UK, Philippines, Germany, Japan. Hybrid-friendly with core collaboration days.

mission.value: To enable motion control solutions that advance exploration, defense, and quality of life through engineering excellence and innovation.

pace_of_work.value: Measured, milestone-driven (program increments 6–18 months). Sprints exist but are paced to hardware integration cycles. Crunch only near flight reviews or test campaigns; otherwise predictable.

products.value: Flight control actuators, satellite propulsion components, industrial motion controllers, medical infusion pumps, flight simulators, and space vehicles. The portfolio spans hydraulic, electric, and hybrid actuation with embedded software and model-based design tooling.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15 days PTO + 10 holidays + 9/80 yields 26 extra days off/year. Carryover up to 5 days. No unlimited PTO.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual year-end shutdown (Dec 24–Jan 1) + July 4 week at some sites. Not guaranteed company-wide but widely observed.

size_stage.value: Public (NYSE: MOG.A, MOG.B); ~$3.3B revenue, ~13,000 employees globally. Mature, profitable, low-turnover engineering culture.

culture_vibe.value: Collaborative, mission‑focused, and humble. Clinicians and technologists work side‑by‑side; decisions are consensus‑driven. Leadership emphasizes psychological safety and continuous learning.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Elite / Tier 1 (National Lab). Equivalent in research prestige to a FAANG AI lab (like Google DeepMind or Meta FAIR) but within the government sector, making it a top destination for applied energy AI.

business_model.value: NLR operates as a government-owned, contractor-operated Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC). It receives annual appropriations from the U.S. Department of Energy and generates additional revenue through sponsored research agreements with industry partners.

culture_vibe.value: Mission-driven and collaborative. The environment is defined by a strong sense of public service and scientific integrity, supported by deep cross-functional teams with academia and industry, rather than internal competition or hyper-growth.

customers.value: As a national laboratory, NLR's primary customer is the U.S. federal government, specifically the Department of Energy. Secondary stakeholders include industry partners, other national laboratories, academic institutions, and policymakers who leverage its research.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $95,000–$115,000 base salary. While national lab salaries are below venture-backed AI startups, they offer premium total compensation for new graduates via guaranteed cost-of-living adjustments, no unpaid overtime, and a massive 5-10% 401(k) match/contribution.

industry.value: Renewable Energy and National Laboratory Research

interview_focus.value: Candidates should be prepared to discuss advanced machine learning and data science concepts applied to energy or physical systems. The interview will likely probe for deep technical rigor and mission alignment, while behavioral questions will verify a candidate's desire for a collaborative, R&D-driven culture over a fast-paced corporate environment.

locations.value: The primary campus is located on a self-contained site at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado.

mission.value: The lab is committed to an affordable and secure energy future. It serves as the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Moderate and steady research pace. Work is centered on deep scientific investigation and multi-year grants, avoiding the rushed sprint cycles of commercial tech. Bureaucracy exists around procurement and security, not product delivery.

products.value: NLR produces scientific research, technical analysis, and pilot-scale energy system demonstrations. Its primary outputs are published findings, data sets, and innovative technologies that can be commercialized by industry partners, rather than consumer products.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days of annual paid vacation leave for incoming professionals, plus separate sick leave. Federal employees and M&O contractors typically accrue leave at generous fixed rates. (This excludes shutdown days).

shutdowns.value: Estimated: The lab likely has a formal holiday shutdown between Christmas and New Year's, along with other federal holidays. FFRDCs commonly guarantee these 'free' days off without charging PTO, ensuring predictable extended breaks.

size_stage.value: NLR is a large, mature research institution with multidisciplinary teams and state-of-the-art facilities. It is a non-profit entity with significant government backing and a long-term, stable operational stage.

customers.value: Individual consumers seeking life insurance and retirement solutions, families needing financial protection, businesses offering employee benefits, and institutional investors accessing asset management services.

locations.value: Headquarters: New York, NY. Major offices: Dallas TX, Philadelphia PA, Chicago IL, San Francisco CA, Boston MA, Atlanta GA, Minneapolis MN. Hybrid work model with office hubs.

mission.value: To provide financial security and peace of mind to policyholders through prudent risk management and long-term value creation, guided by mutual ownership that aligns company interests with policyholder interests.

pace_of_work.value: Measured: Regulatory compliance and actuarial rigor require thorough validation. Projects move in quarters not sprints. However, digital transformation initiatives have accelerated pace in specific innovation teams.

products.value: Life insurance (term, whole, universal), annuities (fixed, variable, indexed), long-term care insurance, mutual funds, ETFs, retirement plan services, and institutional investment management through NYL Investments.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 20-25 days PTO + 10-12 company holidays + 2-3 volunteer days. Additional actuarial study leave (5-10 days). Carryover limits apply.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual year-end shutdown typically Dec 24 - Jan 1 (6-8 business days). Summer shutdown rare but some teams get July 4th week flexibility.

size_stage.value: Large mature enterprise: ~$600B+ in assets under management, ~12,000+ employees, 175+ years operating history, Fortune 100 company, highest financial strength ratings (AAA/Aaa).

summary.value: The New York State Office of Mental Health (OMH) operates psychiatric centers and community-based mental health programs across New York State. technical_work.value: Estimated: Involves traditional IT operations, electronic health record (EHR) management, healthcare data compliance, and state data infrastructure. Fast-paced, elite AI and data science innovation is not typically associated with state agencies.

business_model.value: Revenue comes primarily from tuition and fees, research grants and contracts, medical center operations (NYU Langone Health), endowment distributions, and philanthropic gifts. As a nonprofit, surplus is reinvested in the university's mission.

culture_vibe.value: Intellectual, collaborative, mission-driven. Hierarchy exists (faculty > staff) but labs function as apprenticeship communities. Diverse, global student body. Bureaucracy present (HR, procurement, IRB) but research groups largely self-govern.

customers.value: Students (degree-seeking and continuing education), research sponsors (federal agencies, foundations, industry), patients at NYU Langone, and philanthropic donors.

locations.value: Primary campus in Greenwich Village, Manhattan; Brooklyn campus (Tandon Engineering); NYU Abu Dhabi; NYU Shanghai; global academic centers in 11+ cities; NYU Langone Health campuses across NYC.

mission.value: To be a top-quality international center of scholarship, teaching, and research, retaining and attracting outstanding faculty and encouraging them to create programs that draw outstanding students.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Moderate. Academic research cycles (paper deadlines, grant cycles) create bursts, but no on-call rotations or product shipping pressure. Faculty and research staff set own schedules within grant deliverables.

products.value: Academic degree programs (undergraduate, graduate, professional), research output and publications, continuing education certificates, and clinical services through NYU Langone Health.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 20-22 vacation days + 12-14 university holidays + winter shutdown (~10 business days) = ~42-46 days total annual paid time off for regular staff. Faculty have no formal PTO but control schedules.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Yes — university-wide winter shutdown (typically Dec 24-Jan 2); many labs observe reduced summer hours. No guaranteed 'summer Fridays' but flexible norms.

size_stage.value: Large, mature nonprofit university: ~60,000 students, ~20,000 faculty, ~25,000 staff across multiple campuses; annual budget over $10B including the medical center.
