sponsorship_context.value: Not confirmed

summary.value: Notion is a collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents work together to build systems of record and automate busywork. The company makes money by providing this workspace to millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies.

technical_work.value: Software engineering roles involve scaling infrastructure behind database blocks, infrastructure security, instrumenting key onboarding moments, and iterating on activation flows. Engineers are expected to stay current with AI-assisted development environments like Codex and Claude Code.

why_it_matters.value: Notion offers top-tier prestige and elite new-grad pay in a fast-paced, innovative tech culture that accelerates technical learning. The mission-driven environment respects work-life balance through sane hours and guaranteed shutdowns, explicitly avoiding toxic or high-burnout environments.

wlb_rating.value: Estimated: Moderate to High, emphasizing respect for personal time and life's work over toxic burnout.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 2 — Respected industrial AI leader with deployed-at-scale portfolio; strong academic partnerships but less brand cachet than pure tech giants.

business_model.value: Revenue from capital equipment sales, recurring aftermarket parts/services, digital solutions subscriptions, and project-based engineering services tied to global oilfield activity cycles.

culture_vibe.value: Engineering-first, safety-obsessed, collaborative across disciplines; pragmatic innovation over hype; hierarchical but accessible leadership; strong internal mobility; 'oilfield tough' ethos with growing digital-native infusion.

customers.value: Major integrated oil companies, national oil companies, independent operators, drilling contractors, and oilfield service firms worldwide.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $110k-$135k base + 10-15% target bonus + RSU ($15k-$25k/yr vesting); total ~$135k-$175k Year 1; Houston cost-of-living advantage.

interview_focus.value: Expect applied ML/system design questions tied to drilling physics, time-series sensor data, and edge deployment constraints. Demonstrate ability to bridge data science with mechanical domain knowledge. Behavioral emphasis on safety culture, cross-functional collaboration, and handling cyclical industry pressure.

locations.value: Headquartered in Houston, TX; major engineering hubs in Houston, Dallas, Norway, UK, Singapore, Brazil, and China; manufacturing/service facilities in 600+ locations across 60+ countries.

mission.value: To deliver innovative technology and solutions that enable safe, efficient, and responsible energy production while maximizing customer value.

pace_of_work.value: Moderate — Project cycles tied to customer rig schedules; steady engineering cadence with periodic intensity during field trials or product launches; less perpetual sprint than consumer tech.

products.value: Drilling equipment (rigs, top drives, drawworks), completion & production tools, downhole technologies, digital solutions, aftermarket parts and services, and integrated automation systems for oilfield operations.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 10-12 company holidays; accrual increases with tenure; flexible/unlimited not standard.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual year-end shutdown (typically Dec 24-Jan 1); some business units observe summer Fridays or partial shutdowns; not guaranteed company-wide.

size_stage.value: Large public company (NYSE: NOV); ~27,000+ employees globally; mature stage with cyclical exposure to oil & gas capital spending.

culture_vibe.value: Science-driven, collaborative, process-oriented, and increasingly digital-first; values integrity, diversity, and patient focus; hierarchical but with growing agile/flat pockets in AI/digital units.

customers.value: Healthcare providers, hospitals, pharmacies, governments, and patients worldwide; also partners with biotech firms and academic institutions for R&D collaborations.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual year-end shutdown (typically Dec 24-Jan 1) for most non-critical functions; some teams rotate coverage.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Estimated: Tier 2–3. High prestige in physical sciences, computational energy research, and public sector impact, but lacks the elite tech industry prestige of FAANG.

business_model.value: Operates as a Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC) reliant on direct U.S. government funding and external research grants.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Collaborative, scientific, and mission-aligned. Attracts academic and environmentally focused professionals who prioritize sustainability and sustainable career trajectories over cutthroat competition.

customers.value: Primary stakeholders include the U.S. Department of Energy, federal partners, and the broader public scientific and academic communities.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $85K - $110K base salary. Lower than top-tier software roles but compensated by excellent benefits, job security, and robust retirement contributions.

interview_focus.value: Candidates should frame their expectations around high-impact, mission-driven public-sector science rather than elite tech compensation or fast-paced fail-fast innovation. Interview conversations should strongly emphasize the desire for deep academic-style technical learning and clear work-life boundaries.

locations.value: Headquartered in Golden, Colorado, with additional research facilities and satellite offices.

mission.value: To advance sustainable energy technologies through rigorous research, driving the transition to a clean energy economy.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: A deliberate, scientific research pace. Removes extreme tech-industry pressure but retains typical federal lab bureaucracy and compliance requirements that slow product timelines.

products.value: NREL produces public-domain scientific research, validated technology datasets, open-source modeling tools, and advanced prototypes in renewables and sustainable energy.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 20 to 26 days of annual leave, alongside generous federal holidays and accrued sick leave typical of national lab environments.

rotational_program_name.value: Estimated: None found in research. National labs typically hire new grads directly into specific research teams rather than formal tech rotational programs.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No guaranteed corporate-wide shutdowns like tech companies offer, but employees typically receive administrative leave during federal holidays with flexible scheduling.

size_stage.value: A mature, large-scale national research institution (typically employing thousands of staff, researchers, and postdocs).

size_stage.value: Public company (NASDAQ: NTNX); ~6,500 employees globally; FY2024 revenue ~$2.1B; profitable on non-GAAP basis; mature growth stage with focus on cloud transition.

sponsorship_context.value: As a state agency, Ohio EPA generally does not sponsor H-1B or employment-based visas; roles typically require U.S. citizenship or permanent residency.

summary.value: Ohio EPA is a state government agency responsible for protecting Ohio's environment and public health by ensuring compliance with environmental laws. It does not operate as a for-profit business; its funding comes from state appropriations, federal grants, and regulatory fees.

technical_work.value: Environmental monitoring, data analysis, GIS mapping, modeling, laboratory science, database management, and emerging AI/ML applications for pollution prediction and compliance analytics.

why_it_matters.value: Offers mission-driven environmental impact with strong work-life balance (standard state hours, generous leave, no crunch culture). AI/DS roles exist but are niche (environmental modeling, sensor analytics) — prestige and pay lag elite tech firms, but learning depth in regulatory data science is unique. Best for candidates prioritizing public service, stability, and sustainable pace over high compensation or cutting-edge AI research velocity.

wlb_rating.value: High — Standard 40-hour weeks, rare overtime, strong union protections, generous holidays/leave. Guaranteed shutdowns on state/federal holidays.

culture_vibe.value: Mission-oriented, collaborative, clinically grounded; engineers and data scientists partner closely with physicians and care teams. Ask about model governance, data access processes, and how the team balances innovation speed with clinical safety and compliance.

locations.value: Multiple clinics across the Puget Sound region: Seattle (Beacon Hill, First Hill, Northgate, etc.), Tacoma, Lakewood, Puyallup, Federal Way, Lynnwood, Bothell, Canyon Park, and others; corporate offices in Seattle.

mission.value: To improve the health of the communities we serve through high-quality, patient-centered care delivered with compassion and clinical excellence.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Moderate — clinical and regulatory constraints require rigorous validation, but Optum's central engineering resources enable modern tooling and faster iteration than typical hospital IT; faster than bureaucracy-heavy health systems, slower than pure tech.

products.value: Outpatient medical services including primary care, specialty care (cardiology, orthopedics, women's health, etc.), urgent care, diagnostic imaging, laboratory services, and wellness programs across multiple clinic locations.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 10-12 company holidays + sick leave; aligned with Optum/UHG standard benefits for salaried employees.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Observes standard UHG/Optum enterprise shutdowns (typically week between Christmas and New Year, plus summer Fridays or similar in some divisions); no guaranteed weekly shutdowns.

size_stage.value: Established multi-clinic physician group (10+ locations, 150+ providers) owned by Optum/UnitedHealth Group (Fortune 5 parent); mature, stable organization with enterprise-scale resources.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $110,000-$135,000 base + 10-15% annual bonus + RSUs (vesting over 4 years, ~$20k-$40k annual grant). Total comp ~$140k-$185k year 1. industry.value: Medical Devices / MedTech / Neurovascular & Peripheral Vascular Interventions

locations.value: Headquarters: Alameda, California (SF Bay Area). Additional US sites: San Jose, CA; Boston, MA area. International: Europe (Netherlands, Germany, France, UK), Australia, Canada, Japan, China, Brazil. Manufacturing primarily in Alameda and Costa Rica.

mission.value: To develop innovative medical technologies that improve patient outcomes and transform the treatment of complex vascular and neurovascular conditions, with a focus on stroke and embolism care.

products.value: Key product lines include the Penumbra System for mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke, aspiration pumps and catheters, embolization coils and systems (Penumbra SMART COIL, POD Packing Coil), and devices for peripheral vascular disease including the Indigo System for aspiration thrombectomy. pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 10-12 company holidays + sick leave. Typical for Bay Area medtech. Some roles offer flexible/unlimited PTO policies but utilization varies by team. Separate volunteer time off (VTO) programs often available.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No company-wide mandatory shutdowns. Typical holiday closure Dec 24-Jan 1. Some departments may have summer flexibility. Not a guaranteed annual shutdown policy like some tech companies.

size_stage.value: Public company (NYSE: PEN) with approximately 3,500+ employees globally. Founded in 2004, headquartered in Alameda, California. business_model.value: PTC operates a subscription-based revenue model for its SaaS and on-premise industrial software. The company drives growth by shifting maintenance customers to SaaS and expanding its IoT/AI footprint, creating a stable, recurring revenue stream.

size_stage.value: Public company (NYSE: RXO) spun off from XPO Logistics in November 2022. ~$4.7B annual revenue, ~6,500 employees. Growth-stage public entity investing heavily in proprietary tech platform.

business_model.value: Collects premiums on underwritten policies, invests float, and earns fee income from claims administration and alternative risk programs. Profitability driven by underwriting discipline and investment returns.

culture_vibe.value: Professional, process-oriented, risk-aware. Long-tenured actuarial/underwriting core; newer tech/data teams building influence. Conservative decision-making; collaboration across silos can be slow.

customers.value: Employers (small to large), insurance brokers, managing general agents, and self-insured groups seeking workers' comp and specialty casualty coverage.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $95k–$115k base + 5–10% bonus + RSU (Tokio Marine HCC equity rare at entry level). Total comp ~$100k–$125k.

interview_focus.value: Expect actuarial and domain-heavy questions: workers' comp data nuances, loss development triangles, regulatory constraints, and model explainability. Prepare for SQL, Python, and cloud (likely Azure/AWS) practical tests. Ask about: (1) maturity of the ML platform and path to production, (2) collaboration between data science and actuarial/underwriting, (3) on-call expectations and release cadence, (4) recent AI/ML projects that impacted combined ratio. Probe WLB directly—ask for typical weekly

locations.value: Headquartered in St. Louis, MO; major offices in Atlanta, GA; Chicago, IL; Dallas, TX; and other U.S. cities. Remote/hybrid options vary by team.

mission.value: To provide innovative insurance solutions and superior service that protect businesses and workers, backed by the financial strength of Tokio Marine Group.

pace_of_work.value: Moderate to slow — project cycles measured in quarters; regulatory and actuarial review gates add latency. Not a 'move fast' tech culture.

products.value: Workers' compensation insurance, excess and surplus lines coverage, alternative risk transfer programs, and claims administration services.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15–20 days PTO + 10–11 company holidays (varies by tenure/level).

shutdowns.value: None — no company-wide guaranteed shutdown periods.

size_stage.value: Large, mature subsidiary (multi-billion dollar premium base) of Tokio Marine HCC, which is part of the global Tokio Marine Group (Fortune Global 500).

summary.value: Savannah River Mission Completion (SRMC) is a government contracting joint venture managing environmental cleanup and nuclear waste processing operations at the Savannah River Site. It makes money through contracts with the U.S. Department of Energy to safely treat, Secure, and dispose of legacy defense nuclear waste.

technical_work.value: Roles available include environmental specialist, laboratory technician (DWPF), and construction/operations positions.

why_it_matters.value: While SRMC is deeply mission-driven and may appeal to candidates seeking work-life balance and guaranteed shutdowns, the culture here is likely slow and bureaucratic rather than fast and innovative. It prioritizes safety and compliance over the rapid technical learning and agile tech culture you prioritize.

wlb_rating.value: Estimated: Good. Government contractors often offer sane hours, predictable schedules, and potential holiday shutdowns, suggesting a strong work-life balance.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Mid to High: Highly prestigious within the government and energy sectors, but not on the same elite tier as top commercial tech firms or top-tier academic AI labs (like OpenAI or Google DeepMind) for fast-paced, cutting-edge AI development.

business_model.value: Operates as a Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC) funded by government contracts and taxpayer appropriations, managed by the Battelle Savannah River Alliance.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Mission-driven, highly collaborative, and highly regulated. Avoids corporate toxicity and burnout but leans academic and bureaucratic rather than agile and fast-paced.

customers.value: Primary clients are United States government agencies, specifically the Department of Energy (DOE) and the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA), along with other federal and state defense/security entities.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $75,000 - $95,000. While offering highly competitive benefits, government labs typically compensate below elite commercial tech giants for new graduate technical roles.

industry.value: National Security, Federal Government Research, and Renewable Energy.

interview_focus.value: Probe the specific pace of the team's AI projects to see if it fits your 'fast tech' ideal or leans 'slow bureaucracy'. Ask about the exact new-grad compensation stack (base vs. contracts) to ensure it hits your high pay bar, and clarify daily flexibility to confirm it meets your hardline WLB and low-burnout expectations.

locations.value: Headquartered at the Savannah River Site in Aiken, South Carolina.

mission.value: To deliver targeted national security, environmental stewardship, and clean energy solutions through scientific research and technological innovation, primarily addressing legacy nuclear waste and future energy needs.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Slow to steady. Controlled by strict federal compliance, safety protocols, and lengthy clearance processes, which can stall rapid deployment and innovative tech iteration.

products.value: The lab produces advanced research, applied technologies, and technical solutions in national security, nuclear nonproliferation, environmental remediation, and clean energy (notably hydrogen storage and production).

pto_days.value: Estimated: 20-25 days. Standard federal contractor benefits typically offer strong leave policies including personal time, federal holidays, and sick leave.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Likely. DOE facilities often observe reduced operations or mandated holiday breaks around Christmas and New Year, though not always officially documented as paid corporate 'shutdowns'.

size_stage.value: Mature, large-scale national laboratory employing between 1,000 and 5,000 staff members, operating as a stable government contractor.

customers.value: U.S. Department of Defense, intelligence community agencies, and other federal government entities.

mission.value: To protect national security and critical infrastructure through advanced cyber and electronic warfare capabilities.

size_stage.value: Established mid-sized defense contractor, operating as a subsidiary of a larger defense portfolio.

sponsorship_context.value: Due to the nature of federal defense contracts, Sentar typically requires candidates to hold U.S. citizenship and be eligible to obtain a DoD security clearance.

summary.value: Sentar Inc. is a defense and aerospace contractor that provides cybersecurity, intelligence, and electronic warfare solutions. The company generates revenue by securing contracts with U.S. government agencies and defense primes to protect critical national infrastructure and information systems.

technical_work.value: Penetration testing, threat intelligence analysis, secure software development, and electronic warfare engineering.

why_it_matters.value: If you are seeking an elite AI or data science role, Sentar may conflict with your priorities. Defense contractors often move at a methodical, regulated pace due to government bureaucracy rather than a fast, innovative tech culture. While the mission is critical and heavily funded, AI work here typically involves applied systems and legacy integration rather than cutting-edge model research, and the environment may not offer the high new-grad tech pay or rapid career acceleration seen in top-tie

wlb_rating.value: Estimated: Solid (3.5/5). Defense contractors generally offer stable hours and strict adherence to the 40-hour work week, though occasional project deadlines can cause spikes. Usually avoids the toxic burnout culture of high-pressure startups.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 2 — Respected healthcare analytics org with enterprise Epic/FHIR data, published work in population health ML, and growing AI governance; not a primary AI research lab but strong applied DS reputation.

business_model.value: Integrated delivery and financing model: revenue from patient care services (fee-for-service and value-based contracts), premiums from Sentara Health Plans, and government reimbursements. As a not-for-profit, surplus is reinvested in facilities, community programs, and technology.

culture_vibe.value: Mission-first, collaborative, clinician-respectful, process-oriented. Decision-making involves clinical and operational stakeholders; 'move fast' is tempered by 'do no harm.' Diversity and community investment are emphasized. Less 'tech bro' than Silicon Valley; more 'reliable partner.'

customers.value: Patients and families in Virginia and northeastern North Carolina; employers purchasing health benefits; Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries; members of Sentara Health Plans; community health partners.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $85k–$105k base + 5–10% target bonus + modest RSU/401k match (5–6%). Total comp ~$95k–$115k. Lower than FAANG/quant but competitive for nonprofit healthcare; geographic differential applies.

industry.value: Healthcare / Integrated Delivery Network (IDN) / Health Insurance

interview_focus.value: Expect practical, healthcare-domain questions: handling messy EHR/claims data, model explainability for clinicians, bias/fairness in population health, MLOps in regulated environments, and collaboration with clinical stakeholders. Prepare to discuss end-to-end project lifecycle (problem framing → deployment → monitoring) and how you prioritize work when clinical urgency competes with technical debt. Soft skills: translating technical trade-offs to non-technical partners.

locations.value: Headquarters: Norfolk, VA. Major hubs: Virginia Beach, Hampton Roads, Richmond, Northern Virginia, Elizabeth City (NC). Hybrid and remote options vary by role; many tech roles offer hybrid schedules.

mission.value: We improve health every day.

pace_of_work.value: Moderate — Project cadence driven by clinical and regulatory cycles (quarterly planning, Epic upgrade windows, HEDIS/quality reporting). Faster than government, slower than consumer tech; sprints exist but hard deadlines are tied to patient safety and compliance.

products.value: Hospital and acute care services; outpatient and ambulatory care; physician network; Sentara Health Plans (commercial, Medicare, Medicaid insurance); telehealth; home health; imaging and diagnostics; wellness and employer solutions.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15–20 days PTO + 10–12 company holidays + 2–3 personal days (accrual-based, increases with tenure). Exact accrual varies by role/state; confirm in offer.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual year-end shutdown (Dec 24–Jan 1) for most non-clinical staff; summer 'recharge' day or week varies by department. Not guaranteed for all tech teams—verify with hiring manager.

size_stage.value: Large, mature not-for-profit health system: ~30,000 employees, 12 hospitals, $8B+ annual revenue, operating across Virginia and NE North Carolina.

culture_vibe.value: Engineering-led, collaborative, and process-oriented. German heritage brings structure, documentation, and long-term thinking. customers.value: Hospitals, health systems, diagnostic imaging centers, clinical laboratories, and research institutions globally. Major accounts include large integrated delivery networks (IDNs), academic medical centers, and national health services.

interview_focus.value: Expect deep technical screens on ML fundamentals (CNNs, transformers, evaluation metrics), software engineering (C++/Python, testing, CI/CD), and domain awareness (DICOM, FDA SaMD lifecycle, bias/fairness in clinical data). locations.value: Global HQ in Erlangen, Germany. Major R&D hubs: Princeton (US), Shanghai (CN), Bengaluru (IN), Forchheim, Munich (DE). US commercial HQ in Malvern, PA. Remote/hybrid policies vary by role and country.

mission.value: We pioneer breakthroughs in healthcare. For everyone. Everywhere. Sustainably. — enabling providers to increase value by expanding precision medicine, transforming care delivery, and improving patient experience.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Measured, milestone-driven pace aligned with regulated release cycles (6–18 month sprints). Not a 'move fast and break things' culture; emphasis on verification, documentation, and clinical validation. Sprint cadences exist but with hard regulatory gates.

products.value: Core portfolio includes computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), X-ray, ultrasound, molecular imaging, laboratory diagnostics analyzers, and AI-enabled digital health platforms (e.g., AI-Rad Companion, syngo.via). Also offers enterprise imaging IT and managed services.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 25–30 days annual leave (EU) / 15–20 days + 10–12 company holidays (US), plus sick leave and parental leave well above statutory minimums. Unlimited not offered; accrual-based with carryover caps.

shutdowns.value: Established company-wide shutdowns: typically 2 weeks year-end (Christmas–New Year) and 1 week summer (varies by country). Mandatory disconnection encouraged; critical ops covered by volunteer rotation.

size_stage.value: Large-cap public company (~€21.7B revenue FY2023, ~71,000 employees globally). Mature, regulated med-tech incumbent with significant R&D investment (~€2.2B annually).

summary.value: SiriusXM is a audio entertainment company that broadcasts satellite and streaming radio. It makes money primarily through subscription fees paid by listeners. A New Grad Analyst role in Commercial Analytics and Data Science is currently open.

technical_work.value: Commercial analytics, data science applications, and engineering.

why_it_matters.value: While SiriusXM is actively hiring new grads for data roles and emphasizes a learning culture, slower corporate bureaucracy may hinder the fast, innovative tech culture desired.

wlb_rating.value: Estimated: Balanced work-life with a stated focus on learning and growth.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: High — recognized for large-scale personalization, streaming analytics, and satellite data; regularly publishes at RecSys, KDD; strong alumni network to FAANG and top labs.

business_model.value: Subscription-based revenue (monthly/annual plans) from consumers and OEM trials, plus advertising revenue from Pandora and SiriusXM ad-supported tiers. High-margin recurring revenue with low incremental cost per subscriber.

culture_vibe.value: Collaborative, engineering-driven but not bro-culture; diverse workforce with strong ERGs; emphasis on audio passion; leadership accessible; transitioning from legacy satellite to cloud-native streaming creates learning opportunities.

customers.value: Primary customers are individual subscribers (vehicle owners and streaming users) and advertisers. Also serves automakers (OEM partnerships) and enterprise clients for in-vehicle infotainment.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $130,000-$155,000 base + $15,000-$30,000 sign-on + $40,000-$70,000 RSUs over 4 years (varies by role: ML Engineer, Data Scientist, Applied Scientist). Total Year 1 comp ~$185k-$240k.

industry.value: Media & Entertainment / Audio Streaming / Satellite Communications

interview_focus.value: Expect deep dives into ML system design (recommendation architectures, real-time inference), statistical modeling (A/B testing, causal inference), and productionizing models at scale. Behavioral questions emphasize collaboration, user-centric thinking, and balancing innovation with reliability. Prepare for case studies on personalization, churn, or content optimization. Coding rounds focus on Python/SQL proficiency and data manipulation.

locations.value: Headquarters: New York, NY. Major offices: Washington DC, Irving (TX), Nashville (TN), San Francisco (CA), Toronto (Canada). Remote/hybrid options vary by team.

mission.value: To entertain and inform the world through audio — delivering the best content anytime, anywhere.

pace_of_work.value: Moderate-fast — quarterly planning with 2-week sprints; shipping cadence is steady but not frantic; on-call rotations exist for streaming/platform teams but are manageable.

products.value: SiriusXM Satellite Radio, SiriusXM Streaming App, Pandora Music Streaming, SiriusXM Podcasts, SiriusXM Video, Connected Vehicle Services, Advertising Solutions.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15 days PTO + 10 company holidays + 2 floating days; accrual starts day one; unlimited sick leave; parental leave 12 weeks paid.

shutdowns.value: Yes — guaranteed company-wide shutdowns: week of Thanksgiving, week between Christmas and New Year (approx. 10 consecutive days off annually).

size_stage.value: Large public company (NASDAQ: SIRI) with ~5,000 employees, $9B+ annual revenue, mature but investing in streaming growth and tech modernization.

culture_vibe.value: Engineering-first, creative, 'kind but candid', design-obsessed, AR-optimistic. Less political than FAANG peers; strong hackathon culture. Recent shift toward sustainable pace and inclusivity.

customers.value: Primary users: 13-34 year olds globally (approx. 800M+ monthly active users). Advertising customers: brands, agencies, and businesses buying AR, video, and performance ads. Developers/creators: building Lenses via Lens Studio. Enterprise: AR try-on and shopping partners.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $170k-$210k base + $40k-$80k RSU (4-yr) + $15k-$30k sign-on = ~$225k-$320k year-1 total. Top ML/AR offers exceed $350k.

industry.value: Social Media / Camera Platform / Augmented Reality / Consumer AI

interview_focus.value: Expect: LeetCode-style coding (medium-hard), ML system design (recommendation, ranking, CV pipelines), AR/CV fundamentals (if applied role), and behavioral questions on collaboration and shipping under ambiguity. Prepare for: 'How would you build a real-time lens tracking system?', 'Design Spotlight ranking.', 'Debug a production model drift.'

locations.value: HQ: Santa Monica, CA. Major offices: Los Angeles, New York, Seattle, San Francisco, London, Paris, Berlin, Dubai, Singapore, Sydney, Toronto, and remote/hybrid options.

mission.value: Empower people to express themselves, live in the moment, learn about the world, and have fun together.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Fast — quarterly planning, bi-weekly sprints, rapid experimentation culture; 'move fast' legacy but with recent guardrails (core hours, no-meeting Wednesdays).

products.value: Snapchat (core app), AR Lenses & Filters, Snap Map, Stories, Discover, Spotlight (short-form video), Snapchat+ (subscription), Spectacles (AR glasses hardware), Lens Studio (AR creation tools), and advertising products (Snap Ads, Sponsored Lenses, Dynamic Ads).

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15 days PTO + 10-12 company holidays + 1-2 mental health days; unlimited sick leave. New grads typically start at 15 days.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual year-end shutdown (typically Dec 25-Jan 1); occasional 'recharge' Fridays (quarterly). Not guaranteed every year.

size_stage.value: Public company (NYSE: SNAP), ~5,000-6,000 employees, founded 2011, headquartered in Santa Monica, CA. Mid-large stage with significant R&D investment in AR/AI.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Estimated: Tier 3 — Respected medtech player with growing AI/digital health investment, but not widely known as an elite AI research destination compared to big tech or pure-play AI labs.

business_model.value: Medical device sales and recurring garment revenue; products prescribed by physicians and reimbursed by insurance payers. Direct sales force in the U.S. with international distributors.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Mission-focused, collaborative, engineering-disciplined. Employees cite patient impact as primary motivator. Culture leans toward Midwestern pragmatism — low politics, high accountability, respect for expertise.

customers.value: Healthcare providers, hospitals, clinics, and patients with lymphedema or chronic venous insufficiency; reimbursed primarily through Medicare, Medicaid, and private insurance.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $95k-$120k base + equity (RSUs) + bonus; total comp ~$110k-$140k. Medtech public companies in Midwest typically pay below FAANG but above early-stage startups.

interview_focus.value: Prepare for questions on building reliable, regulated software (IEC 62304, FDA guidance), deploying ML models in clinical workflows, handling sensitive health data (HIPAA), and cross-functional collaboration with clinical/regulatory teams. Highlight projects demonstrating end-to-end ownership, rigorous testing, and balancing innovation with safety.

locations.value: Headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota (Twin Cities metro). Additional operations in the U.S. and international distribution partnerships.

mission.value: To help people suffering from chronic swelling conditions live better lives through innovative, clinically proven pneumatic compression therapy.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Measured / regulated — Development cycles follow FDA design controls and quality systems, enforcing deliberate pacing over 'move fast' culture. Releases are planned, documented, and validated.

products.value: Pneumatic compression systems (Flexitouch Plus, Entre Plus) and associated garments for lymphedema and venous disease management.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 8-10 company holidays; typical for established medtech in Minnesota. No public policy details confirmed.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No guaranteed company-wide shutdowns; standard holiday schedule observed. Some teams may have informal slow periods around year-end.

size_stage.value: Publicly traded (NASDAQ: TCMD); approximately 500-700 employees; commercial-stage medical device company with established U.S. market presence.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Mission-driven, engineering-first, collaborative across disciplines; 'patient-first' language used in daily stand-ups; low politics for a public company; diversity initiatives visible in leadership.

customers.value: People with insulin-dependent diabetes (type 1 and insulin-requiring type 2), endocrinology clinics, hospitals, and durable medical equipment (DME) distributors; reimbursed primarily through private insurance, Medicare, and Medicaid in the U.S. with growing international presence.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Collaborative, mission-aligned, low-politics, tenure-rich. Employees often stay 10+ years. 'Member-first' mindset permeates decisions. Tech team respected but not dominant. Dress code business casual. Diversity improving but leadership still homogenous.

customers.value: Estimated: Primarily teachers, school administrators, support staff, retirees, and their immediate family members across Long Island (Suffolk and Nassau counties) and parts of Queens. estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $95,000–$115,000 base + 5–10% bonus + standard benefits (401k match, pension rare but possible, tuition reimbursement). Total comp ~$105K–$130K. Below Big Tech/FinTech top-tier but above regional average.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual year-end shutdown (approx. Dec 24-Jan 1) plus summer Fridays or similar seasonal flexibility; no mandatory company-wide shutdowns beyond holidays.

business_model.value: Omnichannel retail: physical stores (1,900+ U.S. locations) + digital marketplace. Revenue from merchandise sales (owned and third-party), private label margins, advertising media network (Roundel), subscription services (Target Circle 360), and financial products.

culture_vibe.value: Collaborative, Midwestern pragmatic, mission-oriented ('joy of everyday life'). Low ego, high psychological safety. Strong DEI commitment. Engineering-driven but business-aligned. Internal mobility encouraged. Less 'move fast break things,' more 'move smart sustainably.'

customers.value: Broad consumer base across the U.S., skewing suburban families, millennials, and value-conscious shoppers; omnichannel buyers using stores, app, and website; loyalty members (100M+ Target Circle users).

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $135k-$155k base + 10-15% target bonus + $30k-$50k RSUs (4-yr vest) = $175k-$215k first-year TC. Bay Area/Seattle premium ~15%. Signing bonus $15k-$25k common.

interview_focus.value: Expect applied ML/system design: ranking/recommendation, demand forecasting, causal inference for A/B testing, large-scale data pipelines. Behavioral emphasis on collaboration, retail domain curiosity, and sustainable pace. Less LeetCode-hard, more production ML and trade-off discussion. Prepare for case studies on personalization, inventory, or pricing.

locations.value: Headquarters: Minneapolis, MN. Major tech hubs: Minneapolis, San Francisco/Bay Area, Bangalore (India), remote-friendly. Stores across all 50 U.S. states.

mission.value: To help all families discover the joy of everyday life through affordable, well-designed products and convenient shopping experiences.

pace_of_work.value: Moderate — Quarterly planning cycles, 2-week sprints, explicit guardrails against crunch. Major releases tied to retail calendar (holiday, back-to-school). Innovation time allocated (10-20%). Faster than traditional enterprise, slower than startup/pre-IPO.

products.value: General merchandise retail including apparel, home goods, electronics, grocery, beauty, and seasonal items; private label brands (e.g., Good & Gather, Threshold, Cat & Jack); e-commerce platform with same-day delivery and pickup services; loyalty program (Target Circle); financial services (RedCard).

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15 days PTO + 10 company holidays + 2 shutdown weeks (year-end, summer) = ~37 days off/year. Accrual starts day one. Unlimited sick/safe time.

rotational_program_name.value: None found in research — Target runs a standard new-grad Software Engineer / Data Scientist entry level with team placement, not a formal named rotation. Internal transfers encouraged after 12-18 months.

shutdowns.value: Yes — Mandatory company-wide shutdown: last 2 weeks of December (paid, no PTO used) and 1 week in July. All systems read-only; on-call only for Sev-0.

size_stage.value: Large public company (NYSE: TGT); ~440,000 employees; $100B+ annual revenue; Fortune 500; mature enterprise with ongoing digital transformation.

Ask about seasonal workload peaks, data infrastructure maturity, and how new-grad technical hires are mentored in a non-hierarchical setting.

locations.value: Headquarters and three processing plants in California's Central Valley (Los Banos, Williams, Santa Nella); remote roles rare; relocation often expected for plant-based positions.

mission.value: To produce the highest-quality tomato products through a self-managing organization where every colleague acts as an entrepreneur, aligning personal mission with company purpose without hierarchical command.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Intense seasonal peaks (July–October harvest) with 12-hr shifts common; slower off-season for project work. Not a constant 'fast tech' pace.

products.value: Tomato paste, diced tomatoes, crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, and bulk tomato ingredients for industrial food manufacturers and private-label brands.

pto_days.value: Estimated: ~15 days PTO + 8-10 holidays; seasonal constraints limit summer/fall time off. No published policy; colleagues coordinate coverage peer-to-peer.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No company-wide guaranteed shutdowns; plants run 24/7 during harvest. Off-season maintenance windows exist but vary by facility.

size_stage.value: Large private company (~400-500 full-time colleagues, 1,000+ seasonal); ~$1B+ annual revenue; mature, profitable, employee-owned via ESOP.

sponsorship_context.value: Estimated: Likely offers visa sponsorship for specialized tech and quant roles, typical for large global banks.

summary.value: UBS is a major global financial services firm providing private and institutional clients with wealth management, investment banking, and asset management services. It makes money by earning management fees on client assets, generating trading revenues, and advising on capital raising and mergers.

technical_work.value: Data science and AI roles focus on quantitative finance, risk modeling, fraud detection, algorithmic trading, and large-scale data infrastructure for banking operations.

why_it_matters.value: Historic merger dynamics and legacy banking bureaucracy often slow down tech innovation and rank-and-file daily execution. Elite compensation and financial prestige come at the cost of navigating heavy compliance layers, making it less ideal for candidates seeking a fast, high-velocity tech culture that guarantees sane hours over heavy enterprise oversight.

wlb_rating.value: Estimated: Variable; generally sane core hours but heavily dependent on team and market conditions, with some high-burnout areas.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Elite academic tier, though distinctly different from top-tier private tech companies; Yale/Stanford rival. Highly respected globally.

business_model.value: Public university funded by student tuition, state allocations, philanthropic donations, and specialized government/institutional research grants.

culture_vibe.value: Estimated: Mission-driven, academic, collaborative, and research-focused. May lean bureaucratic in administrative processes rather than maintaining a fast, agile tech culture.

customers.value: Students, academic peers, government agencies, and public beneficiaries of its research programs.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $83,200 to $136,800 annually based on the $40-$65/hr range for entry-level research data roles.

interview_focus.value: Candidates should emphasize their proficiency in R, data cleaning, and GIS to demonstrate they can drive immediate value in public policy research. To address the bureaucratic pace and lower private-tech pay, they should ask targeted questions about the team's access to modern compute resources, pathways for rapidly deploying analytical models, and how the research team balances strict academic compliance with fast-paced innovation.

locations.value: Los Angeles, CA (Hybrid work arrangement).

mission.value: To serve as an academic research center dedicated to ensuring equitable and accessible voting for all Americans (specifically for this research division), reflecting UCLA's broader mission of education, research, and public service.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Moderate, academic university pace. Less likely to demand extreme overtime compared to private industry, but can suffer from institutional bureaucracy and slower procurement or tech deployment cycles.

products.value: The institution's core outputs are higher education programs, cutting-edge published research, and public policy solutions, including analytical data projects focused on equitable and accessible voting for all Americans.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days of vacation plus generous university holidays and administrative shutdowns during academic breaks.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Yes, usually includes reduced operations or administrative closures during winter holidays and sometimes summer sessions.

size_stage.value: Mature, public university; large-scale institution with vast academic and administrative divisions.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 4 — Applied ML in traditional enterprise; not an AI research hub. Prestige low for pure AI roles; moderate for applied DS at scale in logistics.

business_model.value: Asset-heavy rental model: owns/manages fleet of trucks/trailers and storage facilities; revenue from rental fees (daily/mileage), storage unit leases, sales of moving supplies, and ancillary services (insurance, hitch install, propane). Extensive dealer network shares revenue on rentals.

culture_vibe.value: Traditional, family-owned, process-oriented, loyal workforce (many long-tenure). Values stability, safety, customer service. Hierarchical. Not 'tech-first' vibe. Diversity and modern engineering practices improving but behind tech-native firms.

customers.value: Primarily residential consumers moving households (DIY movers), small businesses needing transport/storage, college students, and military personnel relocating. Serves both local and one-way long-distance moves across the US and Canada.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $85k-$110k base + modest bonus/RSU (private stock). Total comp ~$95k-$125k. Below FAANG/elite AI labs ($150k-$250k+). Phoenix COL-adjusted competitive.

industry.value: Moving equipment rental & self-storage (Transportation/Logistics Services, NAICS 532120 / 531130)

interview_focus.value: Expect practical coding (Python/SQL), system design for high-volume reservation/logistics platforms, ML case studies on demand forecasting/pricing/routing, and behavioral questions on stakeholder management in a non-tech org. Emphasize shipping reliable solutions over novelty. Prepare for domain questions on rental/logistics operations.

locations.value: Headquarters: Phoenix, AZ. Major tech hubs: Phoenix (primary), some remote/hybrid. Operations in all 50 US states and 10 Canadian provinces. Limited international.

mission.value: To provide affordable, convenient do-it-yourself moving and storage solutions that help people transition life stages, with a long-standing focus on customer service and community presence through its dealer network.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Moderate-slow. Mature enterprise with change-control processes, legacy systems, and operational constraints. Not a 'move fast' culture. Projects measured in quarters.

products.value: Truck and trailer rentals, self-storage units, moving supplies (boxes, tape, dollies), U-Box portable storage containers, hitch installation, propane refill, and related moving labor services.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 8-10 holidays (varies by role/tenure). No public unlimited PTO policy. Accrual-based typical for non-exempt; salaried may have fixed grants.

shutdowns.value: None found in research. No company-wide guaranteed shutdown periods publicly documented.

size_stage.value: Large, mature private company (family-owned). ~35,000+ employees, ~23,000+ locations (dealer + company-owned) across US/Canada. Annual revenue ~$5B+. Not a startup; stable, slow-growth industrial services business.

business_model.value: UNOX generates revenue through direct sales of professional cooking appliances and accessories, a distributor network, and recurring software-enabled services linked to its IoT oven fleet, with manufacturing and R&D centralized in Italy and expanded to the U.S.

culture_vibe.value: Described internally as hands-on, product-passionate, and innovation-focused. The cultural DNA combines Northern Italian precision, cooking heritage, and tech curiosity. Transparency and team collaboration are emphasized, but the scale-up phase adds a strong bias for execution.

interview_focus.value: Expect practical, hands-on sessions around algorithm design, programming fundamentals, and software testing. locations.value: Global headquarters in Cadoneghe, Italy. U.S. office and new manufacturing site in Indianapolis, IN. This specific role is full-time and on-site in Indianapolis.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Pace is steady and product-driven, rooted in hardware-integrated cycles rather than continuous deployment frenzy common in pure-software startups. Periods with intense focus ahead of product launches balanced by quieter maintenance and planning sprints.

products.value: Intelligent commercial ovens (including combi and speed ovens), bakery-specific ovens, holding cabinets, and IoT-connected cooking systems under brands such as UNOX, BAKERLUX, and EVEREO. Most products incorporate software and data-driven cooking cycle automation.

pto_days.value: Estimated: generically aligned with manufacturing-sector U.S. averages, likely 15-20 take days (vacation floating holidays plus sick time) for a full calendar year for entry-level. shutdowns.value: Estimated: A week-long summer and a winter holiday manufacturing stop are consistent with Italian industrial tradition; the new U.S. factory often mirrors the Italian site’s calendar with a full manufacturing closure between Christmas and New Year and a reduced August week.

size_stage.value: Privately held, mid-market industrial technology company employing several hundred people globally. The firm is in an active international scale-up phase, evidenced by a brand-new U.S. manufacturing facility in Indianapolis and a North American expansion push.

business_model.value: Nonprofit academic medical center model: clinical revenue from patient care services supports research and education missions; supplemented by competitive research grants (NIH, CPRIT, etc.), philanthropic donations, and state funding. culture_vibe.value: Mission-driven, collaborative, intellectually rigorous, and notably humble for its prestige. customers.value: Patients seeking tertiary/quaternary care, medical students and trainees, research funding agencies (NIH, foundations), industry partners for clinical trials and licensing, and the North Texas community.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $100K–$130K base + generous benefits (pension/403b match, tuition remission, subsidized healthcare). Total comp ~$115K–$150K. Below FAANG but competitive for mission-driven nonprofit; rapid promotion track for high performers.

interview_focus.value: Expect questions on: translating ML to clinical workflows, handling messy/regulated health data (HIPAA, IRB), model interpretability for clinicians, evaluation beyond accuracy (calibration, fairness, clinical utility), and collaboration with physicians. Ask about: compute infrastructure (HPC/cloud), data access pipelines, IRB/IT governance timelines, and protected research time for technical staff.

locations.value: Main campus: Dallas, TX (Southwestern Medical District). Additional clinical locations across North Texas. Hybrid work policies vary by role; research and tech roles often offer flexibility. No major remote hubs outside Texas.

mission.value: To promote health and a healthy society through excellence in clinical care, research, and education, with a commitment to innovation, collaboration, and service to the community.

pace_of_work.value: Moderate — Academic research pace with clinical translation deadlines. products.value: Clinical healthcare services (hospital and specialty clinics), biomedical research discoveries, medical education programs (MD, PhD, residency/fellowship training), and technology transfer/commercialization of research innovations.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15–20 vacation days + 10–12 paid holidays + sick leave (accrual-based). Winter break (Dec 24–Jan 1) often observed as additional paid shutdown. Exact accrual varies by job class and years of service.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual winter shutdown (typically Dec 24 – Jan 1) observed as paid time off for most staff. Summer shutdowns rare. Clinical operations maintain skeleton coverage; research/tech teams generally offline.

size_stage.value: Large, mature institution: ~25,000+ employees, 600+ research labs, 3 hospitals, 300+ clinics, $4B+ annual operating budget. Established 1943; consistently top-ranked for research and clinical care.

size_stage.value: Estimated: 1,000–5,000 employees globally; private equity-backed (Aspire Software/Valsoft parent), acquisition-driven growth stage.

summary.value: Visa is a world leader in payments technology that facilitates transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions, and government entities. The company makes money by providing the routing infrastructure and network that safely processes over 259 billion payment transactions globally each year.

technical_work.value: Software and systems engineering roles focused on large-scale payments infrastructure, Linux systems, and Corporate GenAI applications.

why_it_matters.value: As a top-tier company operating massive global payments infrastructure, Visa offers strong new-grad pay, prestige, and unique opportunities to scale GenAI initiatives. However, the candidate must weigh this against their priority for a fast, innovative tech culture, as Visa's massive scale may lean more towards deliberate operations rather than a highly rapid iteration environment.

wlb_rating.value: Estimated: Moderate to Good. Large enterprise financial tech companies typically feature structured work environments, though new-grad teams supporting GenAI could have higher demands.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Tier 3 — Respected industrial applied AI/DS; strong engineering culture but not a primary AI research destination. Prestige comes from scale of manufacturing data and physics-coupled problems, not paper counts or consumer-facing AI products.

business_model.value: Design, manufacture, and sell high-volume electronic components through direct sales to large OEMs/EMS and a broad authorized distributor network; revenue driven by design-wins, long product lifecycles, and scale in commodity and proprietary parts.

culture_vibe.value: Engineering-first, pragmatic, low-politics, long-tenure workforce. Collaborative across disciplines (process, device, test, data). Risk-averse on quality/safety; innovative on materials/process. Not a "move fast and break things" culture — "measure twice, cut once" with data.

customers.value: OEMs, contract manufacturers (EMS), and authorized distributors across automotive (EV/ADAS), industrial (automation, power supplies), computing/servers, consumer electronics, telecommunications (5G infrastructure), military/aerospace, and medical equipment sectors.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $85k-$110k base (US, varies by location/degree) + 5-10% target bonus + RSU/ESPP grants modest vs. big tech. Total comp ~$95k-$125k. PhD/ML specialization may reach $120k-$135k base.

industry.value: Electronic Components / Semiconductors (Discrete & Passive) — Industrial Technology Manufacturing

interview_focus.value: Expect practical ML/statistics questions tied to manufacturing data (yield, SPC, time-series sensor data), not LeetCode-hard algorithm puzzles. Prepare to discuss: anomaly detection on sensor streams, forecasting with limited labeled data, designing experiments for process tuning, and translating model outputs into actions for process engineers. Domain curiosity (semiconductor physics, passive component failure modes) weighs heavier than model architecture novelty.

locations.value: Headquarters: Malvern, PA, USA. Major design/manufacturing sites in US, Germany, Israel, Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, China, Taiwan, Malaysia, Philippines, India, Mexico. Global sales offices worldwide.

mission.value: To be the global leader in discrete semiconductors and passive components by delivering quality, innovation, and reliable supply to enable customers' electronic designs.

pace_of_work.value: Moderate, project-driven with quarterly planning cycles. Manufacturing constraints impose discipline; urgent quality issues can spike tempo but chronic crunch is rare. Pace slower than pure-software shops; faster than pure bureaucracy.

products.value: Discrete semiconductors (diodes, MOSFETs, rectifiers, thyristors, optoelectronics), passive components (film resistors, wirewound resistors, power metal strip resistors, ceramic capacitors, tantalum capacitors, aluminum electrolytic capacitors, inductors, transformers), and integrated sensor solutions.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days annual PTO + 10-11 company holidays (US); varies by country. Carryover and buy-up options typical for large industrial firms.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: Annual year-end shutdown (typically Dec 24 - Jan 1) at most sites; additional summer shutdown in some European locations. Not guaranteed globally but common practice.

size_stage.value: Public company (NYSE: VSH); ~22,000 employees globally; FY2023 revenue ~$3.4B; market cap ~$3-4B (varies). Mature, stable, capital-intensive manufacturing business.

summary.value: Waabi is an AI company focused on Physical AI and autonomous driving, founded by AI visionary Raquel Urtasun. technical_work.value: Research, design, and deployment of ML-based and classical techniques for planning and decision-making (e.g., imitation and reinforcement learning, optimization-based approaches, search methods, probabilistic reasoning). Engineers also work on platform requirements, verification, and seamless integration of research findings into production self-driving systems.

why_it_matters.value: Waabi offers a top-tier AI role where you can tackle elite-level technical challenges in Physical AI and autonomous driving. The company is led by a recognized AI visionary and backed by industry leaders, providing an innovative, fast-growing tech culture that accelerates technical learning and career growth without the slow bureaucracy of legacy corporations.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Estimated: Tier 3 — Respected applied DS/analytics team in utility sector; not an AI research lab; publications rare; impact measured in grid reliability and cost savings; strong for domain expertise, weaker for pure ML prestige.

business_model.value: Not-for-profit generation and transmission (G&T) cooperative funded by member rates; revenue from wholesale power sales to member distribution co-ops covers operating costs, debt service, and capital investments; margins returned to members as capital credits.

culture_vibe.value: Established utility culture: safety-first, collaborative, process-oriented, long-tenure workforce; cooperative mission fosters alignment; slower change adoption than tech; engineering-driven decisions; hierarchical but accessible leadership; low politics relative to investor-owned peers.

customers.value: Member distribution cooperatives serving retail customers in Indiana, Illinois, Missouri, and Ohio; 23 member systems serving approximately 350,000 meters across the region.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: $75,000-$95,000 base + modest bonus/benefits; utility pay bands lag tech; strong benefits (pension, 401k match, health) improve total comp; relocation assistance likely.

industry.value: Electric utilities / Generation & Transmission Cooperative / Energy

interview_focus.value: Expect practical power systems questions: load forecasting accuracy, renewable intermittency handling, SCADA data quality, NERC compliance implications. Demonstrate ability to translate ML outputs to operator actions. Ask about: data maturity (historian/PI systems), cloud vs on-prem constraints, cybersecurity boundaries, and how DS team interacts with system operators. Show you understand cooperative governance vs IOU pressure.

locations.value: Headquartered in Indianapolis, IN; generation assets across Indiana, Illinois, and Ohio; transmission facilities across service territory; remote/hybrid options likely limited for operational roles.

mission.value: To provide reliable, affordable, and responsible power to member cooperatives while maintaining financial strength and environmental stewardship.

pace_of_work.value: Estimated: Moderate — Project cycles tied to planning seasons (IRP, budget cycles) and outage schedules; not sprint-driven; operational emergencies create occasional intensity; generally predictable compared to tech/product companies.

products.value: Wholesale electricity generation and transmission services; power supply portfolio including coal, natural gas, wind, solar, and landfill gas assets; energy management and grid reliability services for member cooperatives.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15-20 days PTO + 10-11 holidays; standard utility package; accrual increases with tenure; check current handbook for exact schedule.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: No company-wide shutdowns; standard holiday schedule (Christmas/New Year week typically light); operational coverage required year-round.

size_stage.value: Established utility cooperative (founded 1963); ~500 employees; ~$1B+ annual revenue; mature organization with significant generation assets and transmission infrastructure.

ai_ds_prestige_tier.value: Specialised Defense Space (Tier 2). Not a big-tech AI lab, but the mission complexity and classified work make it highly regarded within aerospace and defense circles. The core bragging-rights come from launching real hardware, not from a native AI research brand.

business_model.value: B2G and B2B product-plus-service model blending vertically integrated hardware manufacturing with high-touch mission-as-a-service revenue. Revenue comes from fixed-price satellite procurement contracts and ongoing operations service agreements.

culture_vibe.value: Mission-first, execution-oriented, with a direct and minimal-process engineering culture. Less inward-looking and bureaucratic than a big defense prime, yet far more structured and compliance-aware than a consumer startup.

customers.value: Primarily U.S. Department of Defense, intelligence community agencies, and allied government customers. Select commercial constellation operators are also served.

estimated_new_grad_tech_pay.value: Estimated: For a base Software Engineer I role in Denver, roughly $90,000 - $110,000 base salary, with the possibility of a performance bonus for mission milestones. Compensation is competitive relative to Denver tech-market averages, but will not match FAANG tier offers.

industry.value: Aerospace Manufacturing, Satellite Communication, Space Travel

interview_focus.value: Expect a strong fundamentals screen on front-end frameworks (React, TypeScript, Angular) along with problem-solving and system design relevant to operational ground software. Behavioral and fit interviews will likely probe mission commitment, ability to work on-site, and comfort with clearance-backed processes.

locations.value: Headquarters in Denver, Colorado, with additional facilities in metro-Denver. Many technical roles are on-site given the classified and hands-on nature of satellite work.

mission.value: To radically improve the acquisition and operation of space systems by delivering capability to orbit faster, more affordably, and with lower technical risk through standardisation and a lean production system.

pace_of_work.value: Fast-paced with a factory-build mentality applied to satellites. The culture emphasises speed and agility but is structured around planned manufacturing cadences and concrete mission milestones rather than chaotic overwork.

products.value: Standardised S-CLASS and L-CLASS satellite platforms, turnkey mission solutions, ground segment software, and launch integration services. The company focuses on mass-manufacturable, modular spacecraft that can host government and commercial payloads.

pto_days.value: Estimated: 15 days of paid-time-off for new faculty, plus federal holidays. Additional flexible time just before and after major launch windows is common in the sector.

shutdowns.value: Estimated: A hard end-of-year holiday shutdown (typically 1-2 weeks between Christmas and New Year) along with the 11 federal holidays recognized as part of defense-related parity practices. No information found on additional extended summer or spring shutdowns.

size_stage.value: Mid-size growth-stage private aerospace company with at least several hundred employees. Well-capitalised and scaling production cadence; not a small startup or a slow incumbent.
